result.assessment: File coverage is close to complete: every source file under crates/, apps/desktop/src-tauri, apps/desktop/web-rs/src, docs/ and .github/ fell inside one of the 26 slices, and the only partially read regions are test tails (core/scoping.rs tests, graph sharepoint.rs test module), CHANGELOG entry bodies, both Cargo.lock files, and ~20 bindings files that were parity-scanned rather than read. The blind spots are lenses, not files, and the repo shows concrete evidence for each: (1) concurrency across run kinds — cancel_bulk's doc (bulk.rs:125-135) asserts audit and bulk "never run at once" while audit_cancel is claimed in six command files and CancelFlag::cancel deliberately stops every older generation, so cross-kind collateral cancellation is plausible and unexamined; (2) launch-time duplication — Home mounts five LocalResources at sign-in and list_credential_expirations re-pages all of /applications with its own $select instead of reading the app index, alongside the search-corpus prefetch and F007's ungated list; (3) error UX end to end — the frontend branches on ~6 of ~30 UiError codes, reads `retryable` at one site, auth emits `network` while every client emits `network_error`, `throttled` has no rendering, and only the Graph client sets a connect_timeout; (4) install-format-blind updater — check_for_update/perform_update have no MSI/.deb gate although the README says MSI is not auto-updated and the Linux updater only supports AppImage, plus the unsigned-macOS + keychain-ACL question; (5) observability — one `error!` and 65 `warn!` across the backend, no Graph request-id/client-request-id capture (Exchange transport is the lone model), no frontend log persistence, diagnostics commands are cache-only; (6) the ~300 inline tests in the desktop crate could not be executed and nobody assessed whether they would have caught the ~20 confirmed bugs in the same files. Category-wise, perf is under-represented (10 of 439) and several backend findings imply frontend work nobody scoped (F027/F058 exchange unavailability, F059/F178 truncation, F035 terminal events, F073 dead UI branch, F094 revoke UI, F127/F402 marker groups) while F376/F377 need backend DTO changes — the judge should pair these across areas.

result.area_summary:
Slice: error code → producer → on-screen rendering, plus degraded-network behaviour across the IPC boundary.

CODE INVENTORY (producer → rendering):
- refresh_missing / not_signed_in — From<AuthError> (dto lib.rs:159-161) and token_adapter passthrough (http_error.rs:131-133) → `report_if_session_dead` toast with "Re-authenticate" action (errors.rs:54-66); only where a caller routes through it (F353/F427 already cover the gaps).
- consent_required — From<AuthError> only when pre-acquired via `ensure_*`; flattened to `token_error` inside client calls (F110) → `report_consent_required` toast + ~20 hand-rolled `e.code == "consent_required"` branches (scope_wizard, sharepoint_sites_section, usage_panel, panels.rs, …).
- cancelled — audit.rs:334, backup.rs:270 → dr.rs:81 neutral toast, audit → AuditFailure::Cancelled; sign_in hint exists but AuthError::Cancelled is never built (F113).
- forbidden — every client 403 → panels.rs:39 Callout (with consent_required); everywhere else verbatim `e.message` (Graph: raw body, F290; Exchange/KV/ARM: `{err}\n\n{hint}`).
- usage_unavailable / ca_unavailable / activity_unavailable — usage.rs:247, graph_err::premium_feature_err → Callout info/warn with the crafted message; no Retry (tab Refresh button suffices).
- throttled — client 429 after 3 honoured Retry-After waits → verbatim "throttled (429); retry after Some(N)s" / "…Nones" (Debug formatting, finding 1); no "Graph is throttling, wait" wording anywhere except the audit/DR progress notice driven by the throttle observer.
- network_error — reqwest send failure → verbatim "network: error sending request for url (…)" with the cause dropped (finding 2); retryable=true but no Retry offered by the toast sink.
- unauthorized — client 401 incl. the CAE "re-auth needed" path → verbatim "unauthorized (401)" (+ "Sign out and back in" hint for Exchange/KV/ARM), no action (finding 4).
- server_error, graph_error/arm_error/vault_error/exchange_error, deserialize_error, protocol_error, token_error, io, serde, updater, partial_failure (BulkError), and the 16 validation literals (invalid_pfx, cert_is_active, no_scope_group, invalid_redirect_uri, invalid_path, invalid_secret_window, invalid_certificate, cert_generation_failed, invalid_federated_credential, bad_request, unresolved, not_found, application_not_found, sp_not_found, cancelled, updater) → verbatim message, unbranched.
- Sign-in set (network, keyring, authorization, token_exchange, loopback, state_mismatch, url, serde, io, unknown_auth) → sign_in.rs `recovery_hint`: specific hints only for network/keyring/authorization/consent_required/token_exchange/cancelled; the rest get "Check your network and try again".

Sink shapes (grep counts): 56 `error.set(Some(e.message))`, 17 `<DetailLoadError>` (always shows Retry, ignores `retryable`), 12 `report_command_error*`, 11 `Callout{e.message}`, 13 `toast_error(...)`; `.retryable` is read at exactly one site (permissions_tab.rs:121). Special treatment exists only for: the two re-auth-fatal codes, consent_required, cancelled (dr.rs), forbidden (panels.rs), the three *_unavailable, and the sign-in set.

Degraded network: Graph is the only client with `connect_timeout(10s)`; ARM/KV/Exchange (60 s total) and Log Analytics (120 s total) retry network failures 3× under `with_retries`/the hand-rolled Exchange loop, so a SYN-blackholed host costs ≈4×60+7 s ≈ 4 min (LA ≈ 8 min) of skeleton/spinner with no cancel, then a cause-less "network: error sending request for url". Auth token endpoint: 30 s, no retry (F111). Offline at launch: `restore_session` maps a network failure to `Ok(None)`, so the operator lands on the sign-in card with no offline cue and a valid refresh token still in the keyring.

Answers: (1) table above; (2) no — Retry-After is never shown and the message leaks Rust `Option` Debug formatting; (3) `retryable` is effectively dead on the wire — the central sink cannot replay, `use_command` holds `op` as FnOnce; the flag itself is still reasonable advice after three automatic retries; (4) a mid-session `AuthError::Http` during token refresh becomes `token_error` (non-retryable, message "token: http: error sending request…") because token_adapter flattens every non-reauth code; (5) `unauthorized` is deliberately not re-auth-fatal (reauth.rs test) but the UI then renders it as text with no action even though the transport comment says "surfaces to the caller to re-auth"; (6) `.form-error`, `.alert`, `.signin-error` have `white-space: pre-wrap`, `.toast__message` does not, so hints delivered through the central toast sink collapse into one run-on paragraph; (7)-(8) see findings 6 and 7.

findings.title: `throttled` error message leaks Rust `Option` Debug formatting ("retry after Some(30)s" / "retry after Nones") and never says to wait
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:76-77
            #[error("throttled (429); retry after {retry_after_secs:?}s")]
            Throttled { retry_after_secs: Option<u64> },

crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/error.rs:25-26
    #[error("throttled (429); retry after {retry_after_secs:?}s")]
    Throttled { retry_after_secs: Option<u64> },

crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:133-138 (no_hint form used for GraphError)
                    UiError {
                        code: err.ui_code().to_string(),
                        retryable: err.is_retryable(),
                        message: err.to_string(),
                    }

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/ui/detail_load_error.rs:35
            <Body1 class="form-error">{message}</Body1>
findings.rationale: `{retry_after_secs:?}` is the Debug formatter for `Option<u64>`, so the string every client (Graph via the macro, Exchange by hand, ARM/KV via the macro) hands the UI is literally `throttled (429); retry after Some(30)s` or `throttled (429); retry after Nones`. `ui_error_from!` copies `err.to_string()` into `UiError.message`, and DetailLoadError / the toast sink render it verbatim, so after `with_retries` has already exhausted three Retry-After waits the operator reads Rust internals instead of "Microsoft Graph is throttling; wait N seconds". No frontend site branches on `throttled`, and the GUI fixtures use the friendly string `"Too many requests"` (tests/gui/credentials_dashboard.rs:36, managed_identities.rs:68) that the backend never produces, so no test can see the leak. This is not a documented trade-off; the http_retry docs go to lengths to honour Retry-After exactly but the value never reaches the screen in readable form.
findings.proposal: Replace the derived Display for the `Throttled` arm in `http_error_enum!` (and the hand-written `ExchangeError`) with a manual `impl Display` fragment: `Some(n)` → "{api} is throttling requests (429). Wait {n} s, then retry."; `None` → "{api} is throttling requests (429). Wait a moment, then retry." (the macro already has `api_display`, so the API name is available). Add a unit test in `arm`/`keyvault` error-conformance tests asserting the message contains neither "Some(" nor "None", and change the two GUI fixtures to the real backend string so the rendering is pinned end-to-end.

findings.title: Network errors drop the cause: reqwest 0.13 `Display` prints only "error sending request for url (…)", so every `network`/`network_error` message hides DNS/timeout/TLS/proxy
findings.rationale: Since reqwest 0.12 the `Display` impl no longer appends `source()`, so `err.to_string()` yields `error sending request for url (https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications?$top=999)` for a DNS failure, a connect timeout, a TLS interception failure and a proxy 407 alike. The desktop shows this verbatim via DetailLoadError / toast (`network: error sending request for url (…)`), and the sign-in card shows `error [network]: http: error sending request for url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/…/oauth2/v2.0/token)` with the generic hint. The one piece of information an operator behind a corporate proxy needs ("connection timed out" vs "dns error" vs "invalid peer certificate") is available on `reqwest::Error` (`is_timeout()`, `is_connect()`, `source()` chain) and is discarded at all six construction sites. README/F247 asks for proxy/TLS guidance; without the cause on screen, that guidance cannot be matched to a symptom.
findings.proposal: Add one helper in `azapptoolkit-core` (gated off wasm32, next to `http_retry`): `pub fn describe_transport_error(e: &reqwest::Error) -> String` that emits a class prefix (`timed out` / `could not connect` / `request failed`) and walks `std::error::Error::source()` to append the root cause ("dns error: failed to lookup address…", "connection refused", "invalid peer certificate…"). Use it at the six `Network(err.to_string())` sites (Graph transport ×2, ARM, KV, Exchange ×2) and in `AuthError::Http`'s Display (`#[error("http: {}", describe(.0))]` or a manual impl). Expect the operator-facing string to become e.g. `network: could not connect (connection timed out) — https://graph.microsoft.com/…`. Add a unit test with a reqwest error built from a refused localhost port asserting the cause appears.

findings.title: `UiError.retryable` is dead on the wire: the central toast sink never offers Retry and `use_command` discards the operation, so 112 of 113 error surfaces ignore the flag
findings.rationale: The DTO contract says `retryable` advises a retry button, every client computes it via `is_retryable_code` (throttled/server_error/network_error), and the toast primitive supports a sticky Retry action — yet the only consumer is the admin-consent button in permissions_tab. `report_command_error_for` always passes `None`, and the pinning test (state/mod.rs:722-731) asserts a `network` error with `retryable: true` gets no action. errors.rs:70-74 explains the sink cannot replay because it receives only the `UiError`, but `CommandState::run_toast_err` *does* hold `op`; it just types it `FnOnce` so it cannot be re-invoked. Net effect: a 429/5xx/network failure on any of the ~24 `run`/`run_toast_err` call sites and the ~56 inline `error.set(Some(e.message))` sites is a 10-second auto-dismissing red toast (errors without an action are not sticky, toast.rs:129) with no way back except finding and re-clicking the control — the exact "dead end" the module docs say the sink exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: In `use_command.rs`, take `op: impl Fn(String) -> Fut + Clone + 'static` (or `Rc<dyn Fn(String) -> Fut>`) for `run`/`run_toast_err` and, when `e.retryable`, pass a `ToastAction` that re-runs `self.run_with(...)` with the same `on_ok`/`op` into `session.report_command_error_for(&e, feature, Some(retry))` (add an `Option<ToastAction>` parameter; `report_command_error` keeps `None`). Update the state/mod.rs pin to assert the opposite for `retryable: true`. Alternatively, if the team prefers not to replay, drop the "retry button" sentence from the `UiError` doc and remove `retryable` from the wire so the flag stops implying behaviour that does not exist.

findings.title: `unauthorized` (client 401, including the CAE "re-auth needed" path) renders as bare "unauthorized (401)" with no action; the three ui_hints tell the operator to sign out, contradicting the in-place recovery design
findings.rationale: `unauthorized` is deliberately excluded from `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (reauth.rs:64-81) so a fan-out keeps going — that rationale is about halting loops, not about what the operator sees. On screen a Graph 401 (revoked token, CAE challenge the silent re-mint could not satisfy) is the text `unauthorized (401)` in a toast or `unauthorized (401) [unauthorized] Retry` in DetailLoadError, while the remedy the transport itself names ("surfaces to the caller to re-auth") lives one click away as the top-bar "Refresh token" control (shell.rs:492) whose handler already falls back to `reauthenticate` on a dead session. Meanwhile the Exchange/KV/ARM hints say "Sign out and back in", which AGENTS.md ("A dead session forces re-auth in place… never sign the user out") and the shell comment ("still no sign-out, so the cached lists + audit run survive") explicitly reject, and `premium_feature_err` says "Your session expired. Sign in again" (graph_err.rs:88-91) with no control to do so. F353/F427 cover the *dead-session* codes not reaching the sink; this is the 401 class, which reaches the sink and is still a dead end.
findings.proposal: 1) Extract shell.rs's refresh-token handler into `Session::spawn_refresh_token()` (silent `refresh_session` → on `is_reauth_fatal` fall back to `reauthenticate`). 2) In `report_command_error_for`, add a branch before the plain toast: `if e.code == "unauthorized" { push_toast(Error, "Your access token was rejected — refresh it and retry.", Some("Refresh token"), Some(spawn_refresh_token)) }`. Do NOT add the code to `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES`. 3) Reword the three `Unauthorized` ui_hints and `premium_feature_err`'s Unauthorized arm to "use Refresh token (next to Sign out), then retry" — the Exchange `Forbidden { had_diagnostics: false }` hint already uses exactly that phrasing. 4) Add a GUI test next to tests/gui/reauth.rs asserting an `unauthorized` mock produces a toast with a "Refresh token" action.

findings.title: Toast messages collapse the `\n\n{hint}` guidance Exchange/KV/ARM append — `.toast__message` lacks the `white-space: pre-wrap` that `.form-error`/`.alert`/`.signin-error` have
findings.rationale: The stylesheet documents the contract ("Backend UiErrors append actionable guidance after a blank line") and honours it for `.form-error`, `.alert` and `.signin-error`, but the central error sink (`report_command_error_for`, `run_toast_err`) and 13 direct `toast_error` calls render through `.toast__message`, which has no `white-space` rule, so HTML collapses `\n\n` to a single space. The Exchange 403 hint is ~400 characters of numbered steps; in a toast it becomes one run-on paragraph glued to `forbidden (403): [Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization] <no body> (request-id: …)`, which is exactly the surface a mutation on the Exchange scoping section, the scope wizard and the bulk bar use. `.dr-view__error` (dr.rs:280/379) has the same gap for the restore/backup error line.
findings.proposal: Add `white-space: pre-wrap;` to `.toast__message` (styles.css:3513) and `.dr-view__error` (styles.css:4116); optionally also `.app-detail__error`. One-line CSS change, no markup or test rename. Consider a GUI assertion that a mocked `forbidden` error with a `\n\n` hint renders two text nodes / a visible break in the toast.

findings.title: ARM, Key Vault, Exchange and Log Analytics clients set no `connect_timeout`, so a firewalled host burns ~4 min (Log Analytics ~8 min) of un-cancellable spinner before a cause-less network error; Graph alone has the 10 s connect budget
findings.evidence:

            // … Without a separate connect budget a host that
            // accepts no connection burns that whole ceiling before the retry

            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
            .build()
            .unwrap_or_default()
findings.rationale: The Graph client's own comment states the hazard precisely — a host that accepts no connection burns the whole total timeout once per attempt — but the fix was applied to Graph only. For a SYN-blackholed `management.azure.com`, `*.vault.azure.net`, `outlook.office365.com` or `api.loganalytics.io` (typical of an egress allow-list that admitted graph.microsoft.com only), each attempt runs to the 60 s ceiling (Linux/macOS; Windows' TCP stack gives up at ~21 s), and every transport retries network failures three times: 4×60 s + (1+2+4) s ≈ 247 s for ARM/KV/Exchange and 4×120 s + 7 s ≈ 487 s for a Log Analytics usage query. Reads have no `CancelToken`, so the operator sees a skeleton / "Loading…" / disabled button for four to eight minutes and then, per finding 2, `network: error sending request for url (…)` with no cause. Graph's worst case on the same box is 4×10 s + 7 s ≈ 47 s. The SSO metadata probe's `unwrap_or_default()` additionally falls back to a `reqwest::Client::default()` with no timeout at all if the builder ever fails.
findings.proposal: Add `.connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))` to the four builders (arm/client.rs, arm/loganalytics.rs, exchange/client.rs, keyvault/client.rs) and to the SSO probe (and replace `unwrap_or_default()` with the `expect("reqwest client builds")` the other four use so a builder failure cannot silently yield an unbounded client). Better: add `azapptoolkit_core::http_client::builder(total: Duration) -> reqwest::ClientBuilder` that sets user-agent, total timeout, connect_timeout and pool_idle_timeout once, and have all five clients call it, so the budgets cannot drift again (a repo_invariants scan for `reqwest::Client::builder()` outside core would pin it). Effect: worst case drops from ~4–8 min to ~47 s per call, matching Graph.

findings.title: Offline at launch is indistinguishable from "no saved session": `restore_session` folds a network failure into `Ok(None)`, so the sign-in card appears with no offline cue and steers the operator into an interactive sign-in that cannot work while a valid refresh token sits in the keyring
findings.rationale: The documented rationale ("the card is the recovery, and it already says what to do") holds for the cases the comment lists — nothing stored, a revoked token, a locked keyring — where the correct next step really is to sign in. It does not hold for the case the comment omits: the token endpoint is unreachable (laptop off-network, captive portal, proxy down). The refresh token is still valid (only `InvalidGrant` purges it), yet the operator is told to "Sign in to your tenant"; clicking opens a browser that cannot load login.microsoftonline.com, the loopback listener then waits up to 300 s (F113) and returns `loopback`, whose hint is the generic fallback. Nothing on screen ever says "you appear to be offline", and there is no way to retry the silent restore once connectivity returns short of restarting the app. The backend already computes the code (`UiError::from(err).code`) and throws it away.
findings.proposal: Return the classification instead of flattening it: change `restore_session` to `Result<RestoreOutcome, UiError>` where `RestoreOutcome::{Restored(TenantContext), NoSession, Unreachable{code,message}}` (or keep `Option` and return `Err` only for `network`/`token_exchange`-with-5xx). In `Root`, on `Unreachable` render `SignInScreen` with an extra `Callout tone="warn"` — "Couldn't reach Entra ID to restore your session — check your network connection." — and a "Retry" button that re-invokes `restore_session` (not the interactive flow); keep the existing behaviour for `NoSession`. Update the demo fixtures (`demo::register_fixtures`) for the new shape, and add a GUI test that mocks `restore_session` with a `network` error and asserts the offline callout + that `sign_in` is not called.

findings.title: A mid-session token-refresh network failure surfaces as non-retryable `token_error` ("token: http: error sending request…"), not `network_error`: token_adapter flattens the transient auth codes as well as `consent_required`
findings.rationale: Extends F110 (which covers `consent_required`). The same outage produces two different classifications depending on where it strikes: during the Graph call it is `network_error` (retryable: true, "network: …"); during the lazy refresh that precedes the call (`provider.bearer()` at transport.rs:498, ~every hour) it is `token_error` (retryable: false) with message `token: http: error sending request for url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token)`. The auth-plane spelling `network` is hinted only on the sign-in card, so mid-session it never receives a hint either. Operators and any future `network_error`-specific UI treatment (finding 3) will miss the refresh-time half of network failures.
findings.proposal: In `token_adapter::token_error`, map `AuthError::Http(_)` → `"network_error"` and `AuthError::TokenExchange(_)` (5xx at the token endpoint, once F111 adds retry) → `"server_error"`, and let `http_error_enum!`'s `Token(t)` arm pass those two codes through as it does the re-auth-fatal ones (a small `TRANSIENT_PASSTHROUGH` slice next to `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES`, or extend `passthrough_code`). Then `is_retryable` and the UI see one `network_error` class regardless of which hop failed. Add the mapping to the F122 agreement test so `From<AuthError>`'s `network` and the adapter's `network_error` are pinned as the intended pair rather than an accidental split.

minor_nits: GUI fixtures use `fixtures::ui_error("throttled", "Too many requests")` (tests/gui/credentials_dashboard.rs:36, tests/gui/managed_identities.rs:68) — a message the backend never emits — so the tests pin a rendering the operator never sees; use the real Display string once finding 1 lands.

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/sign_in.rs:169 fallback hint "Check your network and try again" is also what `state_mismatch` ("possible CSRF"), `url`, `serde`, `io` and `unknown_auth` receive; a CSRF/state error telling the operator to check their network is a confidently wrong instruction the file's own comment (line 176) says to avoid.

DetailLoadError always renders Retry regardless of `retryable` — documented as deliberate (detail_load_error.rs:6-9, frontend-workspace.md:25), so not a finding, but for `forbidden` / `*_not_found` / `*_unavailable` it is a button that reproduces the same failure; passing `retryable` through to relabel it ("Retry" vs "Reload") would cost one prop.

A 429 with `Retry-After: 300` is honoured verbatim up to three times inside `with_retries` (http_retry.rs:48,70-72), so one command can legitimately block for ~15 minutes; that is a documented decision, but the only in-flight throttle cue is the audit/DR progress notice — single-object loads show a bare skeleton for the whole wait.

result.area_summary: Concurrency review of AppState's three CancelFlags (audit_cancel, sweep_cancel, dr_cancel), the single-flight gate, the ConcurrencyThrottle observer, and what the UI can actually run at once. Flag -> run kinds -> UI entry points: audit_cancel = run_audit (Security "Run audit", Home CTA) + all 11 bulk_* commands (BulkActionBar mounted in the Security All-apps pane, every expanded Findings group, App Registrations, SSO certificates dashboard, Bulk Actions page, plus the Create flow) + migrate_application_access_policies (app-detail Exchange scoping section, audit "migrate" dialog; no Cancel button of its own); sweep_cancel = sweep_site_permissions (Resource Access Sites tab AND the per-app site-access panel) + sweep_key_vault_access (Vault access tab) + find_mailbox_reachers (Mailboxes tab); dr_cancel = backup_tenant + restore_tenant (same DR view, independent busy/restoring signals). Because every top-level view is keep-alive (lib.rs:260-296) and every run gates only on its own local signal, cross-kind overlap is reachable on all three flags, and CancelFlag::cancel() stamps `current`, so with audit gen 1 / bulk gen 2 (or the reverse) any Cancel sets cancelled=2 and both `2>=1` and `2>=2` hold: every Cancel button stops every in-flight run of every kind on that flag. The docstrings that justify the sharing ("the two long-running loops never run at once", "the two never run concurrently from the UI") are false premises, not documented trade-offs. Progress channels: bulk-progress is one channel for all bulk kinds and every mounted BulkActionBar subscribes to it, so two concurrent bulk runs interleave in both rows; the sweep channels are per kind, but two site sweeps (Resource Access + per-app panel) can run at once on site-sweep-progress with no single-flight. Single-flight: all four gate keys are `{tenant_id}|...`; sign-out/clear_cache bump the watched generations so an in-flight holder's `*_if_current` refuses — no race bug there. ConcurrencyThrottle: the recovery loop exits within one 30 s tick after the last Arc drops and each FanOutMeter::attach builds its own tracker, but the per-tenant GraphClient has ONE observer slot, so concurrent fan-outs on the same tenant overwrite each other's tracker and ThrottleGuard::drop clears whichever is installed. sign_out prunes only graph/exchange client maps and cancels nothing; the dead-session latch (next bearer() failing) is the sole stop for a run that outlives sign-out.

findings.title: audit_cancel is shared by the read-only audit, every bulk write and the AAP migration, and the UI can run them concurrently, so any Cancel button stops all of them
findings.rationale: Generation arithmetic: audit claims (current=1, token g=1), then a bulk scope-and-strip/delete claims (current=2, g=2). Pressing Cancel in EITHER the posture strip (cancel_audit) or the BulkProgressRow (cancel_bulk) runs cancel(): cancelled = max(0, 2) = 2, and both 2>=1 and 2>=2 hold, so both runs stop. The reverse start order gives the same result. There is no ordering in which cross-kind collateral cancellation does not happen. Consequences: (1) the operator cancels a read-only scan and a tenant WRITE (bulk delete, scope mailbox/SharePoint access, add owner, disable sign-in, AAP migration) halts mid-selection, reporting 'N app(s) were never attempted' for a Cancel they never pressed on it; (2) the operator cancels a bulk run and the audit result comes back cancelled=true, uncached, and the Security strip shows 'This scan was cancelled early — X of Y principals were scored' (security_view.rs:236-246) — a coverage caveat for a cancel that never targeted the scan. The CancelFlag::cancel doc justifies stopping older generations as 'a run that was going to be superseded anyway', which only holds when all runs on a flag are the same kind; the docstrings' 'never run at once' premise is false given keep-alive views and per-component busy signals, so this is not a documented trade-off. The same overlap also means every mounted BulkActionBar's `use_progress_stream(progress, events::bulk_progress)` (bulk_action_bar.rs:391-392) receives BOTH producers' events, so two concurrent bulk rows show interleaved done/total.
findings.proposal: Give each run kind its own identity. Minimal (S): add `bulk_cancel: CancelFlag` and `migration_cancel: CancelFlag` to AppState, point `cancel_bulk` and all `bulk_*` claims at `bulk_cancel`, the AAP migration at its own flag, and pin the command->flag mapping in repo_invariants/cancel.rs (e.g. a `bulk_*` command body must claim `bulk_cancel`, `run_audit` must claim `audit_cancel`). Robust (M): have `claim()` return the generation to the command, emit it in the first progress event (`run_id` on BulkProgress/AuditProgress), and add a `cancel_run(run_id)` command that does `cancelled.fetch_max(run_id)` only when it is the current generation — then each Cancel button stops exactly its own run and progress listeners can filter by run_id, fixing the interleaved bulk-progress rows too. Update the docstrings at bulk.rs:127, bulk.rs:143-145, audit.rs:14 and caching-and-search.md:350 to state the real rule.

findings.title: GraphClient has a single throttle_observer slot, so concurrent fan-outs on one tenant overwrite each other's tracker and ThrottleGuard::drop clears whichever run's observer is installed
findings.rationale: Each FanOutMeter::attach does build its own ConcurrencyThrottle (no shared tracker), and the recovery loop terminates within one 30 s tick after the last Arc drops (Weak upgrade fails -> break), so those two parts are sound. But the observer slot is one `Option` per GraphClient, and the audit, bulk delete/grant/expired-sweep, site sweep and DR backup all run against the same `Arc<GraphClient>` for the tenant. When run B attaches while run A is in flight, A's tracker is silently replaced: A's 429s now halve B's cap and A's own cap never halves again. When either guard drops first, `clear_throttle_observer()` removes the OTHER run's observer for the rest of its life, so a still-running fan-out runs with a fixed cap and no back-off — exactly the 'stale/missing observer' failure the guard exists to prevent, now in the concurrent case the guard's doc never considers. Distinct from F020 (halving window) and F031 (tick ordering).
findings.proposal: Make the slot multi-observer: `RwLock<Vec<Weak<dyn ThrottleObserver>>>`, `set_throttle_observer` pushes, `on_throttle` notifies every live Weak and prunes dead ones, and `ThrottleGuard::drop` removes only its own tracker (`Weak::ptr_eq`). Alternatively keep the single slot but make `clear_throttle_observer` a compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq` against the guard's own tracker) and log when an attach displaces a live observer. Add a unit test in client/tests/transport.rs that attaches two observers and asserts both see a 429 and that dropping one guard leaves the other attached.

findings.title: sweep_cancel is shared by the site sweep, Key Vault sweep, mailbox probe and per-app site panel, all of which can run concurrently from always-mounted panels; one panel's Cancel aborts the others
findings.rationale: The premise 'the two never run concurrently from the UI' is contradicted by the Resource Access module doc: the Mailboxes, Sites and Vault access panels are display-toggled, each with an independent busy signal, so an operator can start a site sweep, flip to Vault access and start a KV sweep, then probe a mailbox — three runs on one flag (and the per-app site panel in an app detail adds a fourth entry point). cancel() stamps `current`, so pressing Cancel on the 20-second mailbox probe also aborts a multi-minute site sweep and KV sweep; each then reports 'scan was cancelled early' (sites.rs:127-128, keyvault.rs:137-138) and is deliberately NOT cached, so the operator loses the whole scan and gets a coverage caveat for a Cancel they aimed elsewhere. Additionally two `sweep_site_permissions` runs (Resource Access Sites tab + app panel) can be in flight at once: both subscribe to `site-sweep-progress` (sites.rs:159, app_site_access_panel.rs:52) so their progress interleaves, and the tenant-wide sweep is paid twice because there is no single-flight on the sweep.
findings.proposal: Split into `site_sweep_cancel`, `keyvault_sweep_cancel`, `mailbox_probe_cancel` (or adopt the run_id cancel design from the audit_cancel finding) and give each frontend Cancel its own command; fix the docstrings at permission_tester.rs:443 and docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:14-15. For the duplicate site sweep, wrap `sweep_site_permissions` in `state.single_flight(&sweep_cache_key(&tenant_id))` with a post-acquire cache re-check so the second caller joins the first's result instead of re-walking every site.

findings.title: sign_out prunes only graph_clients and exchange_clients; kv_clients, arm_clients and la_clients survive sign-out, and no in-flight run is cancelled

result.area_summary: Launch sequence after sign-in (from source): Root chains `get_auth_config` (local) -> `restore_session` (one token-endpoint round trip) -> `set_active_tenant`, which also runs `restore_open_items`. `AuthedShell` then mounts and, in the same tick, fires: (a) shell: `get_organization` (1 GET, uncached) and `check_for_update` (GitHub, not Graph); GlobalSearch issues no IPC until focus (`prefetch_search_corpus`) or typing; (b) OpenItemsWorkspace: one hidden detail pane per restored dock item (up to 8, F370 says unclamped), each firing `get_application_detail` / `get_enterprise_application_detail` / MI detail immediately (4-5 Graph waves each); (c) HomeDashboard, the only visited keep-alive pane, with five LocalResources: `list_applications_with_pairing` (tenant-wide: full `/applications` with `list_row_select` + its OWN full `/servicePrincipals`, no gate, F007), `list_enterprise_applications` (`indexes_cached`: SP index via single-flight + `app_name_index` = a SECOND full `/applications` with `$select=id,appId,displayName` via single-flight), `list_managed_identities` (joins the SP single-flight), `list_credential_expirations` (a THIRD full `/applications` with its own 5-field `$select`, no gate, unpinned store) and `get_cached_audit` (cache-only, sync). Readiness does NOT auto-run at sign-in (its resource lives in ReadinessView; `readiness_reload` is bumped only by the shell's refresh/reauth and the view's own Retry). Cold 5,000-app / ~6,000-SP tenant at 999/page: `/applications` 6 pages x 3 scans = 18, `/servicePrincipals` 7 pages x 2 scans = 14, `/organization` 1 => ~33 serial-paged Graph round trips, plus ~5 per parked dock item (up to ~40 more); the achievable floor with one shared app scan and F007 fixed is 14. (2) `list_row_select` (8 fields) is a strict superset of the credential roll-up's select (5) and of the name index's (3); `apps_pairing` and `credential_expirations` are busted by exactly the same two tiers (`invalidate_app_lists` AND `invalidate_app_credentials` both invalidate both keys), so the roll-up can be produced by the pairing scan; the name index (lists tier only) can be seeded from the same scan with its own per-key watch, exactly as the SP index already is. The caching doc's invariant "exactly two cached tenant-wide directory enumerations, and no surface may run its own" is violated by two launch-path commands. (3) Yes: Home receives the full `AuditRunResult` (up to 10k `AuditItem`s, 21 fields incl. five Vecs) over IPC to compute `posture_counts`/`ranked_actionable_findings`, the audit controller pulls a second copy into `result: RwSignal<Option<AuditRunResult>>`, both re-pull on `audit_reload`, and the backend deserializes the run from the untyped `Value` on every call; Home likewise pulls the full apps/enterprise/MI/credential collections for ~12 numbers. (4) Nothing is needlessly serialized (config -> token -> resources is inherent); parallelism is fine except the redundant scans and the eager hidden-pane fetches; readiness and corpus prefetch stay out of the launch path. (5) `beforeBuildCommand` = `just web-build-release` = `trunk build --release --locked`; wasm gets `wasm-opt=z` + opt-level z/lto/strip, but Trunk's `minify` defaults to `Never` (verified in upstream `src/config/types/minify.rs`) and neither Trunk.toml nor the recipe sets it, so the 120,706-byte styles.css and the wasm-bindgen JS glue ship unminified; no shipped bundle size is recorded in DEVELOPMENT.md / release-updater-demo.md or gated (only debug test shards via `web-itest-size`). (6) A long session retains, per visited pane, its resource values: Home holds full copies of apps rows (~10k), enterprise rows, MI rows, credential rows and the audit run; Security holds a second audit copy plus its lists; up to 8 detail panes hold `ApplicationDetail` + visited tabs. Sign-out (`set_active_tenant(None)`) and any tenant change re-run Root's `match tenant.get()`, unmounting `AuthedShell` and disposing every keep-alive pane, so retention is steady-state duplication, not leakage.

findings.title: Credential-expiry roll-up is stored unpinned although cache.rs names it as a pinned tenant-wide index

findings.title: trunk build --release ships unminified CSS and JS: Trunk's `minify` defaults to `never` and nothing enables it

Trunk.toml:1-6: `[build]\ntarget = "index.html"\ndist = "dist"\n# Optimization is selected by the caller's `--release` flag ... so there is no `release` default to set here.` (no `minify` key)

result.area_summary: Packaging / updater / OS-path lens. Read commands/updater.rs, tauri.conf.json, updater-build.json, release.yml (whole file), the justfile build-* recipes, release-updater-demo.md, README Install/Updates/Opting out/Requirements/Logs, DEVELOPMENT.md packaging + updater sections, web-rs update_splash.rs / shell.rs update code / bindings + DTOs, lib.rs config_directory + tracing, core::private_file, auth::token_cache, commands/export.rs, and the vendored tauri-plugin-updater 2.12.0 (check/get_urls, Windows NSIS/MSI launch, Linux AppImage/deb/rpm, macOS bundle swap), tauri-utils platform::bundle_type and apple-native-keyring-store. Answers to the slice questions: (a) an MSI or .deb install IS offered the update — the plugin looks up `windows-x86_64-msi`/`linux-x86_64-deb` first and then falls back to the bare key release.yml populates with the NSIS/AppImage payload; on MSI the NSIS per-user installer runs beside the per-machine MSI (the duplicate install the README warns about), on .deb the whole AppImage downloads and then fails with the raw plugin error "invalid updater binary format" in the splash. The app CAN know its format: `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` is binary-patched by the bundler and is what the plugin itself consults — `check_for_update` should short-circuit on Msi/Deb/Rpm. (b) The macOS store is the legacy keychain via `set_generic_password` with default ACLs; unsigned/ad-hoc bundles have no stable designated requirement, so each replaced binary triggers a keychain prompt on `restore_session`, which is swallowed to `Ok(None)` and lands on the sign-in card with no explanation. (c) Logs (debug level, 14 daily files) live under `%APPDATA%` (Roaming) alongside settings.json — LOCALAPPDATA is the norm for logs (Tauri's own app_log_dir uses it); the private_file Windows branch is a documented trade-off and acceptable under the per-user profile; export.rs does no path validation at all — the OS dialog's path goes straight to `write_owner_only`, and std handles UNC/`\\?\` paths, so no rejection problem. (d) rpm is advertised nowhere (justfile/DEVELOPMENT.md say "omitted for now"); the real Linux portability problem is the floating `ubuntu-latest` runner: a workspace binary built on this glibc-2.39 host imports `__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38` as a STRONG symbol, so the AppImage/.deb cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04 (2.35), Debian 12 (2.36) or RHEL 9 (2.34) while README/release body say "runs on most distributions". (e) DEVELOPMENT.md claims the NSIS installer "asks once about per-user vs per-machine"; the config has no nsis.installMode, so Tauri's default currentUser applies and nothing asks (README correctly says per-user, no admin). Intel-mac and MSI-not-auto-updated claims are consistent with release.yml.

findings.title: MSI and .deb installs are offered the NSIS/AppImage payload: no install-format gate in check_for_update although bundle_type() is available
findings.rationale: The plugin resolves the download key as `{os}-{arch}-{bundle}` then `{os}-{arch}`; latest.json only carries the bare keys, so an MSI or .deb install gets `Some(update)` and the shell toasts "Update available" on every launch. On an MSI install, clicking "Update & restart" downloads the NSIS setup.exe, `extract_exe` classifies it as Nsis and `ShellExecuteW(setup.exe /P /UPDATE /R)` installs a second, per-user copy beside the per-machine MSI — exactly the outcome README:255-258 tells MSI users to avoid, and the only documented guard is the opt-out that F036/F139 found is never read. On a .deb install, `bundle_type()` is Deb so `install_deb` runs on AppImage bytes, fails `is_deb` after the full download and the raw plugin string "invalid updater binary format" lands in the splash's warn Callout (update_splash.rs:40-43). The manual "Check for updates" menu item (shell.rs:196-208) has the same blind spot. Tauri exposes the install format at runtime — `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` (tauri re-exports `tauri_utils as utils`, lib.rs:115; the bundler binary-patches the `__TAURI_BUNDLE_TYPE` marker) — and the plugin already relies on it. Complements, does not duplicate, F036/F139.
findings.proposal: In `check_for_update` (and `perform_update`), read `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` and short-circuit for `Some(BundleType::Msi | BundleType::Deb | BundleType::Rpm)`. Preferably make the DTO a tri-state (`UpToDate` / `Available(UpdateInfo)` / `ManagedExternally { format }`) so the manual check can say "This MSI/.deb install is updated by your packaging tooling" instead of "You're on the latest version", and the launch check stays silent. Pull the decision into a pure `fn updatable_format(BundleType) -> bool` with a unit test, mock the new shape in the GUI shell test. Alternative worth weighing: publish `windows-x86_64-msi` and `linux-x86_64-deb` keys in latest.json (the plugin can run msiexec /passive and dpkg via pkexec) and drop the "not auto-updated" policy — but that is a policy change; the gate is the safe default.

findings.rationale: glibc symbol versioning binds each import to the default version of the *build* host's libc, and glibc 2.38 redirected `strtol`/`sscanf` to `__isoc23_*` under `_GNU_SOURCE`. The objdump above shows those as strong (non-weak) imports in a binary from this very workspace built on 2.39; the desktop binary additionally compiles aws-lc-sys C code, so its floor is at least the same. `ubuntu-latest` is 24.04 today (glibc 2.39) and will float again to 26.04, so the artifact's minimum distro silently changes with GitHub's runner image. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (2.35, supported to 2027), Debian 12 (2.36) and RHEL 9 (2.34) all fail at load with "version `GLIBC_2.38' not found" — the .deb even installs cleanly first. The README/release body promise the opposite, and nothing in release.yml checks the floor. Tauri's own guidance is to build Linux bundles on the oldest distro you intend to support. Note the AppImage bundling WebKitGTK does not help; glibc is never bundled.
findings.proposal: Pin the Linux matrix leg to `ubuntu-22.04` (or the oldest distro the README promises), and add a post-build guard step in the same job: `objdump -T target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/azapptoolkit | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -Vu | tail -1` asserted <= 2.35 so a runner-image drift fails the release instead of shipping. Document the actual floor ("needs glibc 2.35+, i.e. Ubuntu 22.04 / Debian 12 or newer") in README Linux install and the release-body Row text, and note that the runner pin is load-bearing in release-updater-demo.md. Consider the same pin for the ci.yml Linux jobs only if they produce shipped bytes (they do not today).

findings.rationale: Legacy-keychain items created with `SecKeychainAddGenericPassword` get an ACL naming the creating application. For code without a Developer-ID signature there is no stable designated requirement — the trusted-app entry is bound to the specific binary — so after the updater swaps `/Applications/azapptoolkit.app` (plugin `install_inner`, rename of the bundle) the new binary is a different app to Keychain Services. The next `find_generic_password` in `restore_session` raises the system "azapptoolkit wants to use your confidential information stored in 'azapptoolkit'" dialog; "Always Allow" only lasts until the next update, and "Deny" surfaces as `AuthError::Keyring`, which `restore_session` turns into `Ok(None)` — the operator lands on the sign-in card with no hint that the update caused it, and the subsequent sign-in's `set_generic_password` on the existing item can hit the same ACL again and fail with the misleading `keyring` hint "unlock your keychain". None of this is written down: README/DEVELOPMENT.md cover only the one-time Gatekeeper bypass. Reasoned from Apple's keychain ACL model and the vendored store code; not observed on hardware (no macOS here).

Medium term: treat Developer-ID signing (stable `identifier + team` designated requirement) as the fix rather than only notarization, and say so in the DEVELOPMENT.md macOS paragraph. Optionally, on macOS only, have `restore_session` log the `keyring` code at warn when the stored version in settings.json differs from CARGO_PKG_VERSION, so support can recognise it.

findings.title: Daily debug-level logs (14 files) are written to Roaming AppData on Windows instead of LOCALAPPDATA
findings.rationale: `%APPDATA%` is the Roaming hive; Windows convention (and Tauri's own `PathResolver::app_log_dir`, which resolves to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<identifier>\logs`) puts logs and caches under Local because Roaming is synchronised with roaming user profiles / FSLogix / UE-V at logon and logoff. The MSI is explicitly marketed for SCCM/Intune/GPO estates — the population most likely to roam profiles — and this app writes at `debug` level for its own crates, two weeks of it, so the profile carries megabytes of request logs (with tenant/object GUIDs) between machines and slows logon. settings.json belongs in Roaming (it is per-user config); the logs do not. The comment at lib.rs:333-337 documents the path but gives no roaming rationale, so this is a convention slip rather than a decision.
findings.proposal: Introduce `log_directory()` per platform: Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\azapptoolkit\logs` (fallback to `%APPDATA%` only if LOCALAPPDATA is unset), macOS `~/Library/Logs/azapptoolkit` (the platform convention), Linux `$XDG_STATE_HOME`/`~/.local/state/azapptoolkit/logs` or keep `.local/share` but honour `$XDG_DATA_HOME`. Keep settings.json where it is. Update README Logs + the lib.rs comment, and add a one-line CHANGELOG note since the documented log location changes for operators. Consider a one-time best-effort move of existing log files so support instructions stay valid.

findings.title: DEVELOPMENT.md says the NSIS installer 'asks once about per-user vs per-machine'; the config uses Tauri's default currentUser mode, so nothing asks

DEVELOPMENT.md therefore contradicts both the shipped behaviour and the sibling docs; a contributor who 'fixes' the config to `both` to match the doc would break silent updates for anyone who picked per-machine.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the sentence to "installs per-user with no prompt and no admin rights (Tauri's default `currentUser` NSIS mode — keep it that way: the passive updater relaunch depends on it)". One-line docs edit; optionally pin with a repo_invariants check that `bundle.windows.nsis.installMode` is absent or `currentUser`.

result.area_summary: Observability lens on what a support engineer can reconstruct from the daily-rolling log (lib.rs install_tracing: EnvFilter `info,azapptoolkit=debug,desktop=debug`, 14-day retention, panic hook). Answers to the slice questions, all from reading the code: (1) No `client-request-id` is ever sent to Graph — `send_core_url_with` builds only Authorization/ConsistencyLevel/Prefer/Content-Type headers — and no `request-id`/`client-request-id`/`Date` is ever read from a Graph, ARM or Key Vault response (only `Retry-After` and, for Graph, `WWW-Authenticate`); batch sub-response headers are parsed but only `retry-after` is consulted. The Exchange transport is the lone in-repo model (captures `request-id`/`x-ms-diagnostics`, warns on every 4xx with cmdlet+status+request_id). (2) The Graph transport itself emits exactly one log line in 784 lines (the CAE re-mint failure at info); a terminal 403/404/4xx/5xx-after-budget is never logged in the transport, `From<GraphError> for UiError` (`ui_error_from!(GraphError, no_hint)`) just maps, and the frontend sink (`report_command_error_for` → toast; `use_command.run` → `error` signal) never logs, so a failed write vanishes once it crosses IPC. 15 command files performing writes (remediation, restore, expose_api, app_roles, applications/{credentials,owners,federated,authentication}, exchange/{grants,scope_group,aap_migration}, graph_roles, defaults, config, updater) contain zero tracing calls; bulk.rs logs only join errors. (3) A 429 storm during the audit lands as N copies of `transient failure; retrying label="graph" attempt=… retry_after_secs=…` (http_retry.rs:207) — no endpoint, no status (429 vs 503 indistinguishable, `RetryReason` not logged) — plus `throttle: throttled, reducing in-flight cap` from the observer; inner `$batch` 429 re-batches log nothing. Graph 5xx: same retry line then, if budget exhausted, nothing (the error flows to a toast). (4) Token refresh failure IS well logged (auth/service/mod.rs:174 warn with aad_error, redacted description, correlation_id; :534 `refresh token rejected, purging` with tenant_id). (5) Dead session mid-fan-out: audit logs `audit stopped: session is dead` once (audit.rs:359); other fan-outs latch `SessionDead` silently. (6) A panic inside a `#[tauri::command]` future does reach the panic hook (std hooks are global; tokio's catch_unwind runs after) and lands as `backend panic` with backtrace — but per tauri 2.11.6 `respond_async_serialized_inner` the invoke promise is never settled, so the UI spins forever with no toast. (7) An IPC arg-deserialization rejection is not logged backend-side (tauri's `tracing` feature is off; enabling it would record full request/response bodies at trace, i.e. secrets — not a fix). (8) WASM panics go only to `console_error_panic_hook` → webview console; there is no frontend→backend log command, no tauri-plugin-log, and no devtools in release, so they are unrecoverable. (9) At `azapptoolkit=debug` a 10k-app audit emits ~zero lines per Graph call (no per-request logging at any level); debug output is a handful of cache hit/miss and SP-index lines. PII in the log is limited to app display names in one warn (audit.rs:1497), tenant ids in auth lines, object ids in backup lines — no request URLs/`$filter` values or UPNs are logged. (10) Startup banner logs only version + log_dir; OS/arch, cloud, configured tenant id and profile are absent. (11) The only diagnostics surface is the cache dialog (stats/TTL/clear); there is no 'Open log folder'/'Copy diagnostics' affordance and no bundle command, while README:252 falsely says a failed update check 'is logged'.

findings.title: Graph/ARM/Key Vault transports send no client-request-id and never capture request-id/Date — Microsoft-support correlation is impossible for every non-Exchange failure
findings.rationale: Microsoft Learn ('How to debug Microsoft Graph API calls', 'Best practices for working with Microsoft Graph § Reliability and support') says: generate a unique GUID per request, send it as `client-request-id`, log it, and always log the response `request-id` and `Date` — 'they're required when you report issues ... to Microsoft Support. Without these headers, diagnosing the issue is difficult.' Today a Graph 403 (`forbidden (403): {body}`), a 404, a post-budget 5xx or a 429 surfaces with status+body only; there is no identifier a support engineer can hand to Microsoft, and no log line at all is written for the terminal failure in the transport. The repo's own DEVELOPMENT.md policy ('log the ui_code/request id') is met only by the Exchange client.
findings.proposal: In `send_core_url_with` (and `scoped_get`/`scoped_send_core`, ARM `send_with_retry`, KV `send_core_url`): (a) mint a v4 GUID per logical request (move `commands::guid::new_v4_guid` into `azapptoolkit-core` so the crates can use it; `rand` is already a dependency) and set `client-request-id`; (b) on any non-success capture `request-id`/`client-request-id`/`Date` (ARM: `x-ms-request-id`, `x-ms-correlation-request-id`; KV: `x-ms-request-id`; batch: the same keys from each sub-response `headers` map) and append them to the error detail the way Exchange's `compose_error_detail` does (`… (request-id: …, client-request-id: …)`) so the UiError message and any toast carry them; (c) emit one `tracing::warn!(method, path_without_query, status, request_id, client_request_id, "graph request failed")` at the terminal-failure site (Attempt::Done(Err(..)) paths and budget exhaustion). Pin with a wiremock test in `tests/transport.rs` asserting the request header is present and the ids appear in the error. Effect: every failure in the log and the UI is correlatable by Microsoft support; the 429/5xx question 'which endpoint' becomes answerable.

findings.title: README promises a failed update check 'is logged (see Logs)' but nothing logs it — the launch-check error is discarded on both sides of IPC
findings.rationale: An operator whose fleet never sees updates (proxy blocking github.com, signature mismatch, malformed latest.json) is told by the README to look in the log — and the log is empty. `check_for_update` maps the plugin error straight into a UiError and the launch path pattern-matches `Ok(Some(_))`, dropping `Err(_)` without a trace. This is distinct from F036/F139 (the unread opt-out) and F250 (bug template fields): here the documented diagnostic path does not exist.
findings.proposal: In `updater_err` (or at the two `.map_err(updater_err)?` sites in `check_for_update`/`perform_update`) add `tracing::warn!(error = %e, "update check failed")` / `"update install failed"` — the plugin error Display includes the endpoint status and signature-verification reason and carries no secret. Optionally log `tracing::info!(current, available, "update available")` on `Some(update)`. Effort S; makes README:253 true and gives support a one-line answer to 'why doesn't it update'.

findings.title: Startup panics with zero diagnostics if the log file cannot be created: install_tracing `.expect()`s the appender before any subscriber or panic hook exists
findings.rationale: `create_dir_all`'s error is ignored, then `build()` is unwrapped. On a read-only or unwritable app-data dir (locked-down %APPDATA% redirection, a sandboxed/kiosk profile, HOME unset so the fallback is the install directory) the very first thing the process does is panic — before `install_panic_hook` and before any `tracing` subscriber — so a double-clicked GUI app 'just doesn't open', the advertised log directory holds nothing, and stderr is invisible. The panic hook's own doc comment (lib.rs:374-378) explains exactly why an unlogged crash is unacceptable; this path defeats it.
findings.proposal: Install the panic hook first (it only needs `tracing` macros, which are no-ops until a subscriber exists — or buffer: install a stderr-only subscriber first). Make the file appender optional: `match builder.build(&log_dir) { Ok(a) => Some(non_blocking(a)), Err(e) => { eprintln!(...); None } }`, register the file layer via `.with(file_layer_option)` (tracing-subscriber supports `Option<Layer>`), then after init `tracing::warn!(log_dir = %log_dir.display(), error = %e, "file logging disabled")`. Consider surfacing the same fact in the config screen / About so the operator learns the log is not being written. Effort S.

findings.title: No failure (or mutation) logging at the command boundary: 15 write-command files contain zero tracing calls and the UiError conversion/frontend sink never log, so a failed or destructive operation leaves no trace in the log
findings.rationale: The operator reports 'Remove password failed' or 'the tool disabled sign-in on the wrong app'. The log has nothing: the Graph transport logs no terminal failure, the `From` conversion is a pure map, the toast is ephemeral. Even successful destructive writes (bulk delete, disable sign-in, AAP migration, DR restore) leave no local record of which object was touched when — only Entra's server-side audit log knows, which the support engineer may not have access to. Backend-wide there is exactly one `error!` (the panic hook) and 65 `warn!`s, none on the common command failure path.
findings.proposal: One boundary hook instead of ~50 edits: (1) give the `backend`-feature `ui_error_from!` arms (and `From<AuthError>`) a `tracing::warn!(code = %ui.code, retryable = ui.retryable, source = %err, "command error")` — add `tracing` as an optional dep of `azapptoolkit-dto` under `backend`; body text is already what flows to the UI (F290 covers capping it). (2) Feed the same hook into a small `AppState` ring buffer of the last N UiErrors (code, message, UTC timestamp) for the diagnostics bundle. (3) For mutations, add an `info!` line in the shared write cores that are already single-sourced (`remediate_*` cores, `run_bulk_seq`, `invalidate_app_*` call sites are natural choke points) naming command, tenant id and object id. Pin (1) with a unit test that a `GraphError::Forbidden` conversion emits a warn (tracing-test or a capturing subscriber). Effect: every failed command and every destructive write has a timestamped log line.

findings.title: Webview panics and IPC rejections are never persisted: console_error_panic_hook writes only to the webview console and there is no frontend→backend log command
findings.rationale: F425 documents that any non-UiError IPC rejection panics the whole WASM app. When that (or any other frontend panic — an `expect` in a view, a Leptos runtime error) happens in a release build, the operator sees a frozen or blank window; the panic message exists only in a devtools console that release builds cannot open, so a bug report can contain nothing but 'it went blank'. The backend log, the one artifact support asks for, is silent because nothing bridges the two worlds.
findings.proposal: Add `#[tauri::command] fn log_frontend(level: String, message: String)` (three-step pattern: command, `generate_handler!`, `bindings/diagnostics.rs` stub) that re-emits at `tracing::{warn,error}!(target: "webview", %message)` with a length cap. In `run()`, replace `set_once()` with `std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(|info| { console_error_panic_hook::hook(info); let msg = info.to_string(); leptos::task::spawn_local(async move { let _ = invoke_result::<()>("log_frontend", ...).await; }); }))`. Also call it from `Session::report_command_error_for` for the plain-toast branch so IPC failures the operator saw are in the log with their `code`. Register a no-op fixture in `demo::register_fixtures` (enforced by `demo_fixture_coverage.rs`) and gate the invoke on `not(feature = "demo")` if simpler. Effect: WASM panics and surfaced UiErrors land in the same daily file as backend events.

findings.title: No diagnostics affordance beyond cache stats: no 'Open log folder' / 'Copy diagnostics', no bundle command — operators are told to hand-locate and hand-redact log files
findings.rationale: Support triage today requires the operator to know the platform path, find today's file among 14, guess which lines matter, and redact by hand. The app already holds everything a minimal bundle needs (version, `cache_stats`, the resolved tenant id/cloud, the log directory) but exposes none of it together, and the one dialog that exists is about cache tuning. The bug template's version field even points at a menu that does not exist off macOS (see the docs finding).
findings.proposal: Add `#[tauri::command] fn get_diagnostics_bundle(state) -> DiagnosticsBundleDto` in commands/diagnostics.rs: version, `std::env::consts::{OS,ARCH}`, cloud, configured tenant id, `log_dir` path, `CacheStatsDto`, the last N UiErrors (ring buffer from the boundary-logging finding), and the tail (last ~200 lines) of today's `azapptoolkit.<date>.log` read from `log_directory()`. Frontend: an account-menu item 'Copy diagnostics' that renders it as text and writes it to the clipboard (the clipboard path already exists for secrets) plus a read-only path display 'Log folder: …' with a copy button — no new plugin needed; if an OS reveal is wanted later, `tauri-plugin-opener::reveal_item_in_dir` is the standard route. Update the bug template to say 'Account menu → Copy diagnostics'. Effect: one click produces what the template asks for, already scoped to today and free of hand-redaction guesswork.

findings.title: Retry/throttle log lines carry no endpoint, status or reason — a 429 storm and a 5xx outage look identical, and inner $batch 429 re-batches are silent
findings.evidence:
http_retry.rs:207-212 (the only log line on the retry path):
  tracing::warn!(
      attempt = budget.attempt(),
      label,
      retry_after_secs = ?retry_after_secs,
      "transient failure; retrying"
  );
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:552: `let outcome = with_retries("graph", retry_class, |_| {` — constant label, attempt number discarded, nothing logged inside the closure.
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/batch.rs:283-300 (inner-429 re-batch loop): the only side effect is `obs.on_throttle(max_retry_after)` and `budget.wait(max_retry_after).await;` — no tracing call.
findings.rationale: The task's headline failure mode — a 429 storm during a 10k-app audit — produces N identical `transient failure; retrying label="graph" attempt=1 retry_after_secs=Some(…)` lines plus `throttle: throttled, reducing in-flight cap`. `RetryReason` (Throttled vs Transient) and the HTTP status are not logged, so a Graph 503 incident and a tenant-quota 429 are indistinguishable in the file; the endpoint family (`/servicePrincipals`, `/$batch`, `/sites/{id}/permissions`) is unknown, so the engineer cannot tell which fan-out is being throttled. When the budget is exhausted nothing is logged at all — the error becomes a toast. The `$batch` path, 'the throttle-happiest endpoint in the API' per its own comment, logs no inner retries.
findings.proposal: (1) Log `reason = ?reason` and the retried error's `ui_code()`/status in `with_retries` (E: Display is available; add a `status: Option<u16>` to `Attempt::Retry` or log `%err`). (2) Pass a label that names the request: `format!("graph {method} {path}")` where `path` is the URL with query stripped (`url::Url::path()`) — no `$filter` values, hence no PII; ARM/KV can do the same. (3) In `batch_chunk`, `tracing::info!(throttled = throttled.len(), pending = urls.len(), attempt = budget.attempt(), ?max_retry_after, "$batch: re-batching throttled sub-requests")` and a `warn!` when the budget is spent. (4) When `!budget.may_retry()` log `warn!(label, attempts, "retry budget exhausted")` before returning `Err(err)`. Effort S; all inside `http_retry`/transport, covered by existing paused-clock tests.

findings.title: `target = "azapptoolkit::graph"` / `"azapptoolkit::cache"` are recorded as a field named `target`, not as the event target, while both layers hide the real target with `with_target(false)`
findings.evidence:
service_principals.rs:188-192:
  tracing::debug!(
      target = "azapptoolkit::graph",
      first_page = page.items.len(),
      "service-principal index first page"
  );
Same form at service_principals.rs:209,216,257; commands/applications/mod.rs:143,151; enterprise_application.rs:74,77; managed_identity.rs:57,60; permissions.rs:55,58 (`tracing::debug!(target = "azapptoolkit::cache", kind = "Lists", key = %key, "hit")`).
tracing-0.1 macros.rs:21,55,663: the target override is spelled `target: $target:expr`; `$($k:ident).+ = $($fields:tt)*` is the field arm.
lib.rs:359-365:
  .with(fmt::layer().with_target(false).compact())
  .with(fmt::layer().with_ansi(false).with_target(false).with_writer(file_writer))
findings.rationale: The authors intended a stable logical target so operators could filter `azapptoolkit::cache=debug`; instead each line gains a bogus `target="azapptoolkit::cache"` field, the real target stays the module path, and the intended filter matches nothing. Because both fmt layers set `with_target(false)`, the support file shows no module attribution at all — a `warn` from the graph crate, the auth crate or a command is indistinguishable except by message text (the README's `azapptoolkit_graph=trace` advice works only because the real target is the module path).
findings.proposal: Replace `target = "..."` with `target: "..."` at the 13 sites (compile-checked), and turn `with_target(true)` on for the FILE layer only (keep stdout compact). Add a repo-invariant test that greps for `tracing::\w+!\(\s*target =` to keep the misspelling from returning. Effort S.

findings.title: Startup banner records only version and log_dir — OS/arch, cloud, configured tenant id and build profile are missing, so the first thing support needs is not in the log
findings.evidence:
lib.rs:368-372:
  tracing::info!(
      version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
      log_dir = %log_dir.display(),
      "azapptoolkit starting"
  );
state.rs:248-256 logs the tenant/client id only when they are UNSET (`"AZAPPTOOLKIT_TENANT_ID is not set; sign-in will fail until configured"`); nothing logs the resolved value or its source (env / settings.json / baked). bug_report.yml:36-43 asks the operator to type the OS by hand.
findings.rationale: A log tail sent by an operator should self-describe: which OS/arch (Windows chunked keyring vs macOS), which cloud (sovereign endpoints), which tenant the session was for, whether it is a debug build, and where the ids came from (env override vs settings.json — the README's three-way resolution is a classic support question). Today all of that must be asked back.
findings.proposal: Extend the banner: `os = std::env::consts::OS, arch = std::env::consts::ARCH, debug = cfg!(debug_assertions)`, and after `AppState::new` log `tracing::info!(cloud = ?env, tenant_id = %tenant_id, tenant_id_source = "env|settings|baked", client_id_source = ..., "resolved auth config")` (tenant id is already logged by the auth crate at service/mod.rs:534, so no new exposure). Effort S.

findings.title: The security audit — the app's flagship long run — writes no start/finish summary line (duration, totals, coverage gaps, cancelled), unlike the site sweep
findings.rationale: 'The audit took 40 minutes / stopped at 60% / shows fewer findings than yesterday' are the questions a support engineer gets; the log cannot answer any of them — a fully successful run of 10k apps leaves zero lines, a cancelled run leaves zero lines, and the `degraded` coverage gaps (which the UI correctly refuses to cache) are never recorded. The site sweep already demonstrates the one-line pattern.
findings.proposal: At `run_audit` entry `tracing::info!(%tenant_id, "audit started")`; capture `Instant::now()`; at the end `tracing::info!(total, scored = items.len(), unscored, degraded = ?degraded, cancelled, elapsed_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(), "audit complete")`. Same two lines for `backup_tenant`, `restore_tenant` and the `bulk_*` commands via `run_bulk_seq` (count, failed, cancelled). Effort S.

findings.title: Bug template tells reporters to read the version 'From Help → About', but the Help submenu is empty and exists only on macOS; the version actually lives in the account menu
findings.evidence:
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml:30-35: id: version attributes: label: App version description: From Help → About, or the installer filename. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:238-240 `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")] fn macos_menu(...)` and lib.rs:318: &Submenu::with_id_and_items(app, HELP_SUBMENU_ID, "Help", true, &[])?, (About is under the app-name submenu at lib.rs:274, macOS only; Windows/Linux have no native menu.) apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:468-469:
{concat!("Version ", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))}
findings.rationale: A Windows or Linux reporter following the template finds no Help menu at all; a macOS reporter finds an empty one. The version is displayed in the tenant-pill account menu, which the template does not mention. Complements F250 (which is about the missing install-format field) without overlapping it.
findings.proposal: Change the description to 'Shown at the bottom of the account menu (click the tenant name, top right), or the installer filename.' If the diagnostics-bundle finding lands, point at 'Copy diagnostics' instead. Effort S.

minor_nits: A panic inside a #[tauri::command] future IS logged by the hook (std panic hooks run before tokio's catch_unwind), but tauri 2.11.6 `respond_async_serialized_inner` (ipc/mod.rs:370-388) calls `return_result` only after `task.await` returns, so the invoke promise never settles: `use_command::run_with` never clears `busy` (use_command.rs:64-74) and the UI spins forever with no toast — the `backend panic` log line is the only signal. Consider a frontend watchdog or a `tokio::spawn(...).await` wrapper mapping JoinError → UiError("internal_panic") in the few commands with `.expect()`s (throttle.rs:69/101).

transport.rs:678 (`CAE claims challenge could not be satisfied silently`) is the only tracing call in the entire 784-line Graph transport; success paths log nothing at any level, so `RUST_LOG=azapptoolkit_graph=trace` (README advice) adds essentially no request-level output.

`app.restart()` (updater.rs:71) and `restart_app` (config.rs:64) exit via std::process::exit, so the `WorkerGuard` managed in Tauri state is never dropped — lines still in the non_blocking channel at that instant are lost; a `tracing::info!("restarting for update")` immediately followed by exit may not reach the file. Flush/drop the guard (take it out of state) before restarting.
Non-blocking appender is lossy by default (DEFAULT_BUFFERED_LINES_LIMIT 128_000); harmless at today's volume but worth `.lossy(false)` once per-request logging exists.

PII inventory for the log at default filter: app display names in one warn (audit.rs:1497 `app = %app.display_name`), tenant ids (auth service/mod.rs:534,545), object/SP ids (backup.rs, sharepoint.rs:810). No request URLs or `$filter` values are logged at any level, so user-typed search prefixes and UPNs never reach the file; raw Graph error bodies do (F290).

result.area_summary:
Static test-oracle review of the ~300 inline unit tests in apps/desktop/src-tauri (sso/mod.rs 21, sso/claims.rs 8, audit.rs 19, permissions.rs 17, permission_tester.rs 15, applications/cache.rs 15, applications/credentials.rs 13, gallery.rs 11, cert.rs 11, sharepoint.rs 10, readiness.rs 10, conditional_access.rs 10, restore.rs 7, expose_api.rs 7, bulk.rs 6, remediation.rs 6, backup.rs 4, state.rs 6, lib.rs build_support seam, tests/repo_invariants/commands.rs).

Q1 (why the 20 confirmed bugs slipped past the nearest test): every bug lives in a State-bound or AppHandle-bound body while every test in these files (except credentials.rs:456-597 and backup.rs:1024-1128) exercises a pure helper one layer below. The failure modes split cleanly: (a) the test PINS the bug — claims.rs:442-443 asserts `TransformationID` present / `ID` absent, i.e. F070's wrong shape, via an encoder->decoder round trip with no Microsoft-documented fixture; (b) missing negative/failed-read case — remediation.rs passes `|_, _| false` at all six call sites so the fail-closed veto branch (F022) is dead in the suite; backup.rs:1104 hands `SessionDead::new()` to the only wiremock test and never asserts `is_dead()` (F039); exchange/tests.rs:213-219 feeds only `User.Read.All` to the resolver while tests.rs:81 proves targets include EWS (F054 — two halves tested, never joined); (c) fixture cannot model the failing input — `EntraReach` (permission_tester.rs:177-192) and `Option<Vec<String>>`/`Option<HeldSharePointGrants>` have no 'read failed' representation (F055/F056/F057); `SiteSweepResult` has no `truncated` field (F059, sharepoint.rs:1234-1241); score_one swallows the SP error into a clean `Ok(AuditItem)` so `only_a_complete_undegraded_run_is_cacheable` (audit.rs:1664) tests the guard but nothing tests the producer (F023); (d) asymmetry visible from the test table — `a_signing_certificate_lifetime_is_bounded...` (sso/mod.rs:1787) has no `resolve_secret_lifetime_days` twin because the gate does not exist (F074); managed_identity.rs tests stop at `scope_level` labels, never the per-subscription flatten (F072). F001/F004 are special: `create_application_core`, `grant_single_permission_core`, `grant_admin_consent_core` already take `&GraphClient` (permissions.rs:389, 618) so partial-write wiremock tests need no refactor — nobody wrote them. F037/F038/F071/F075/F025/F026 sit behind `State`/`AppHandle` with no `_core` seam at all.

Q2 (files with tiering/invalidation/fail-closed/latch decisions and zero handler-level tests): F010 is confirmed and extends — `AppState::for_test` appears only at credentials.rs:509/543/565. Zero `MockServer`/`for_test` in sso/mod.rs (6 `invalidate_app_lists` sites: 177, 320, 707, 746, 1662, 1728), audit.rs (latch via `classify_audit_failure` and cache guard at 445, both only pure-tested), sharepoint.rs (cache-on-complete 988-992), restore.rs (Pass 4 `session.is_dead()` at 300, `unwrap_or_default` reads at 734), bulk.rs (4 `invalidate_app_lists` sites 288/393/514/593; its 4 tokio tests drive `run_bulk_seq` with identity closures), permissions.rs, permission_tester.rs, remediation.rs, expose_api.rs, applications/mod.rs (export_tests only). backup.rs has ONE wiremock test but on `GraphClient::with_base_url` (not for_test), covering Pass 1's chunk helper only; Passes 2-3 take `&AppHandle` and cannot be constructed.

Q3 (fixtures): two handler-test client idioms with incompatible base-URL conventions (for_test appends `/v1.0`, backup.rs:1080 does not), backup's `app_json` byte-identical to the graph crate's `tests/common.rs::sample_apps_json`, three copies of the `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` clock, three `RequiredResourceAccess` builders, three `ServicePrincipal` builders, eight per-format CSV formula-injection tests re-checking `export::csv_field` (already tested at export.rs:294). Proposal: `commands/test_support.rs` following graph's `client/tests/common.rs` and the existing `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn csv_columns` precedent.

Q4 (implementation-detail pins): no HashMap-order pins found (all map outputs are compared via `.get()` or iterate Vecs). Prose-matching is forced by untyped errors in conditional_access.rs (two causes, one code `ca_unavailable`), credentials.rs (`Result<_, String>` -> one code `invalid_secret_window`), cert.rs (`Result<_, String>`); markup pins in audit.rs:1960/1976 and sso/mod.rs:2248 are minor.

Q5 (seams): the `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "../build_support.rs"]` mount is the right tool for pure code that must also compile into build.rs and nothing else in the crate has that need. progress.rs's generic `R: tauri::Runtime` buys nothing without `tauri/test` (Cargo.toml:31 `features = []`; no `#[cfg(feature` anywhere under src/ or tests/, so NO test is silently excluded). The proven seam is bulk.rs:46-54 `ProgressSink` (4 driver tests via `Recorder`), but it is private to bulk and re-invented as `report: &(dyn Fn(usize) + Sync)` in backup.rs:364; lifting it into progress.rs is what unblocks handler tests for audit/backup/restore/sharepoint/tester/keyvault_rbac.

New non-test defect found while tracing invalidation tiers: set_saml_urls, set_oidc_redirect_uris and set_claims_mapping bust both tenant-wide indexes via `invalidate_app_lists` for detail-only writes (the F026 pattern, in sso).

findings.title: claims.rs round-trip test pins the F070 wire-format bug: it asserts TransformationID is emitted and ID is absent, with no Microsoft-documented fixture
findings.rationale: An encoder->decoder round trip through one codec is a tautology for a wire format; the only external oracle is Microsoft's documented definition string, and none of the 8 claims tests uses one (contrast `the_two_thumbprint_fields_are_different_encodings_of_the_same_bytes`, which pins `DOC_CKI`/`DOC_THUMBPRINT` copied from Microsoft's reference). Microsoft's sample is `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData",...}` with `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId == "DataJoin"`, so the entry needs BOTH keys. Because the test asserts the wrong shape, the F070 fix will fail this test and look like a regression; a maintainer 'fixing the test' would restore the bug.
findings.proposal: Replace lines 440-443 and 453-455 with `a_transformation_entry_matches_microsofts_documented_shape`: fixture = Microsoft's documented definition string (Source transformation, ID DataJoin, TransformationId JoinTheData, ClaimsTransformation with OutputClaims ClaimTypeReferenceId DataJoin); assert `parse_claims_definition` yields `id == Some("DataJoin")` and a new `transformation_id == Some("JoinTheData")`; assert `build_claims_definition` of that DTO emits both `ID` and `TransformationID`/`TransformationId` (read case-tolerantly) and that the OutputClaims reference resolves to the schema ID. Add the thumbprint test's rule to the module doc: wire-format tests use a Microsoft-documented sample, never a hand-built expectation. Lands with F070's DTO change.

findings.title: Every plan_redundant_removals test passes `|_, _| false`, so the fail-closed veto branch that F022 breaks is dead in the suite; a for_test handler round trip would hit F022 by construction
findings.rationale: The `broader_is_confined` parameter exists only for the fail-closed veto, yet six tests pass a constant `false`, so the veto->skipped contract documented at 373-377 is unasserted and F022 (`continue` with no `skipped.push`) is invisible. `AppState::for_test` has no signed-in tenant, so `exchange_client` returns `not_signed_in`, `mail_scopes` becomes empty, and `broader_is_confined` returns true for every Graph mail permission — a handler-level test would have reported `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }` for an app with Mail.ReadWrite + Mail.Read and made the bug obvious.
