verdicts.notes: Evidence is real: `#[error("throttled (429); retry after {retry_after_secs:?}s")]` at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:76 (shared by Graph/ARM/KV via the macro) and crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/error.rs:26 use the Debug formatter on `Option<u64>`, so the string is literally `retry after Some(30)s` / `retry after Nones`. `ui_error_from!` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:127-128,144) copies `Display` into `UiError.message`; `DetailLoadError` (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/ui/detail_load_error.rs:35) and `.toast__message` (components/toast.rs:179) render it verbatim. No frontend code branches on `"throttled"` (only a bulk-bar unit-test fixture at components/bulk_action_bar.rs:1352), and the GUI fixtures use `"Too many requests"` (tests/gui/managed_identities.rs:68, credentials_dashboard.rs:36) which the backend never emits, so no test sees the leak. Nothing in docs/architecture, AGENTS.md or CHANGELOG documents this as deliberate. Two corrections to the proposal: (a) the macro's `api_display` is the format literal for the `Api` variant (e.g. `"graph error ({status}): {body}"`), not a bare API name, so `"{api} is throttling"` needs a new macro input or generic wording; (b) no manual `impl Display` is needed — thiserror 2.0.21 (Cargo.lock) supports `#[error("throttled (429); {}", retry_hint(.retry_after_secs))]` with a small fn, keeping the derive.

Premise verified against the vendored source: reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:3915-3916) `impl Display for Error` (registry reqwest-0.13.5/src/error.rs:257-304) writes only the kind text (`error sending request`) plus ` for url (…)`; `source()` is exposed separately and never appended. Every construction site discards it: 12 `Network(e.to_string())` sites in total (graph transport.rs:32,47,143,157,571,582; arm transport.rs:60,69; keyvault client.rs:196,205; exchange transport.rs:188,197 — six are send failures, six are body-read failures), plus `AuthError::Http` displays as `http: {0}` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/error.rs:47-48). Only Exchange logs the error with `?err` (Debug, which does include `source`), so the cause reaches the log there but never the UI. Two corrections: the README has no proxy/TLS guidance at all (grep for proxy/firewall/corporate/egress finds nothing; 'F247' is a sibling finding, not repo content), so drop that justification; and `azapptoolkit-core` does not depend on `reqwest` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml:22-26 lists parking_lot/async-trait/tokio/url only), so the proposed `core::describe_transport_error` adds a new (non-wasm-gated) dependency to core — acceptable but should be called out given AGENTS.md's 'dependencies are a cost', or the helper can live in a crate that already has reqwest and be re-used.

The mechanics are real: `.retryable` is read at exactly one site (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:121); `report_command_error_for` always passes `None` (state/errors.rs:160); errors without an action auto-dismiss (components/toast.rs:129); `run_with` takes `op: impl FnOnce` (hooks/use_command.rs:48) so it cannot replay; and state/mod.rs:722-731 pins `retryable: true` → no action. But the 'dead end' framing is overstated: (1) `DetailLoadError` always renders a Retry button for every load failure regardless of the flag (detail_load_error.rs:36-43), so load surfaces are covered; (2) `CommandState::run` (28 call sites) writes the inline `error` signal next to the control that triggered it, so the operator re-clicks in place — only `run_toast_err` (16 sites) and the 15 direct `report_command_error*` callers are toast-only; (3) by the time `throttled`/`server_error`/`network_error` reaches the UI, `with_retries` has already spent MAX_RETRIES=3 attempts honoring Retry-After (core/http_retry.rs), so an immediate manual retry has limited value; (4) errors.rs:70-74 documents why the sink cannot replay. The '112 of 113 surfaces' figure counts inline-error sites that do not need a toast action. Not a documented decision to drop the flag, so the doc/behaviour mismatch is genuine but small.

verdicts.notes: All cited evidence is real. No `"unauthorized"` branch exists anywhere in apps/desktop/web-rs/src, so a Graph 401 (transport.rs:610-611 plain 401; 663-664 and 677-683 CAE re-mint failure) falls through `report_command_error_for` to a plain toast of `unauthorized (401)`. The three `ui_hint`s say 'Sign out and back in' (crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/error.rs:32-35, keyvault/src/error.rs:35-37, exchange/src/error.rs:124-128) and graph_err.rs:88-91 says 'Sign in again', contradicting AGENTS.md ('never sign the user out') and the in-place design already implemented by the shell Refresh-token handler (views/shell.rs:116-146: `refresh_session` → on `is_reauth_fatal` → `reauthenticate`). The Exchange `Forbidden{had_diagnostics:false}` hint already uses the correct 'use "Refresh token" (next to Sign out), then retry' wording (exchange/error.rs:116-122), so the reword is consistent with existing copy. `unauthorized` is correctly excluded from `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (core/reauth.rs:32,64-81) and the proposal preserves that. tests/gui/reauth.rs covers only `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in`, so a new GUI test is the right pin. Severity is at the low end of medium: access tokens refresh ~60 s before expiry so a 401 is an anomaly (revocation/CAE), and the remedy is one click away; the hint reword (S effort) is independently worthwhile even if the toast action is deferred.

Verified: only the Graph client sets `.connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:163-176, with the comment quoted); ARM (arm/src/client.rs:36-40, 60 s), Log Analytics (arm/src/loganalytics.rs:27-31, 120 s), Exchange (exchange/src/client.rs:74-78, 60 s) and Key Vault (keyvault/src/client.rs:54-58, 60 s) set only a total timeout. The Exchange transport retries a send failure `MAX_RETRIES` times (exchange/src/client/transport.rs:178-188); ARM/KV return `Attempt::Retry{Transient}` on send failure (arm/transport.rs:56-61, keyvault/client.rs:192-198), retried for `RetryClass::Idempotent`, so the 4×timeout+7 s worst case holds for reads. The SSO metadata probe's `.build().unwrap_or_default()` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:1282-1285) does fall back to `reqwest::Client::default()`, which has no timeout. No repo_invariants test scans client builders. Two additions: the finding missed a sixth builder — the auth service's token-endpoint client at crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:93-97 (30 s total, no connect_timeout) — and `azapptoolkit-core` has no `reqwest` dependency (core/Cargo.toml:22-26), so the proposed `core::http_client::builder` adds one; a lighter alternative that avoids the dep is a `repo_invariants/sources.rs`-style scan asserting every `reqwest::Client::builder()` is followed by `.connect_timeout(`.

Code path verified: `restore_session` folds every error into `Ok(None)` after computing and logging the code (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:37-44); the frontend ignores `Err` too (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/lib.rs:167-174); the service's restore performs a real refresh-token POST (`access_token_for_scopes`, auth/service/mod.rs:614-617) and only `InvalidGrant` purges the refresh token (mod.rs:529-540), so offline → `AuthError::Http` → token retained → sign-in card. The loopback wait is 300 s (mod.rs:274). However this IS a documented deliberate decision — the command's doc comment (auth.rs:20-31) states `Ok(None)` is the answer for 'every way this can come up empty' and argues a launch-time error toast is noise. The finding's real contribution is that the enumerated cases omit 'token endpoint unreachable', where 'sign in' is not the right next step. Proposal is over-scoped: the demo build skips the restore entirely (`#[cfg(not(feature = "demo"))]` at lib.rs:161-162; no `restore_session` fixture exists in demo/ or tests), so no fixture update is needed; and a new `RestoreOutcome` enum is a wire-shape change touching the binding when the existing `Result<Option<_>, UiError>` already has an `Err` arm nobody uses. Severity low: narrow window (offline at launch), the refresh token survives so relaunching online just works, and the sign-in flow's `network`/`loopback` hints eventually say to check the network.
verdicts.corrected_title: Offline at launch is folded into `Ok(None)`: the sign-in card steers an operator with a still-valid refresh token into an interactive sign-in that cannot succeed, with no offline cue or restore retry
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Keep the command signature. In `restore_session`, compute `let ui = UiError::from(err)` (already done at auth.rs:40) and return `Err(ui)` only when `ui.code == "network"`; every other failure keeps `Ok(None)` and the documented rationale. In `Root` (web-rs/src/lib.rs), capture that `Err` into a signal and render `SignInScreen` with a `Callout tone="warn"` reusing `sign_in.rs::recovery_hint("network", …)` wording plus a 'Retry' button that re-invokes `bindings::auth::restore_session()` (not `sign_in`). Extend the auth.rs doc comment to name the offline case as the one exception. Add a GUI test mocking `restore_session` with a `network` UiError asserting the callout renders and `sign_in` is not called. No demo fixture work is required.

verdicts.notes: Premise verified: `token_adapter::token_error` maps `AuthError::Http(_)` (and everything else non-fatal) to `"token_error"` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/token_adapter.rs:22-27); `passthrough_code` only passes `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/reauth.rs:50-52), so `ui_code()` yields `token_error`; `is_retryable_code` excludes it (core/http_retry.rs:25-27). A network failure during the lazy refresh therefore surfaces as non-retryable `token_error` with message `token: http: error sending request for url (…)`, whereas the same outage during the Graph call is retryable `network_error`. The adapter's own doc ('The codes must match `UiError`'s — `From<AuthError> for UiError` is the source of truth', token_adapter.rs:19-20) is already violated since dto maps `Http` → `("network", true)` (dto/lib.rs:169). Not documented as deliberate. The `TokenExchange → "server_error"` half of the proposal is unsafe and should be dropped: `classify_token_error` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/wire.rs:44-62) returns `TokenExchange` for every AAD error that is not invalid_grant/consent — including permanent 4xx like `invalid_client`/`unauthorized_client` — and `post_token` also returns it for any non-JSON non-success (`HTTP {status}` from a proxy block page, mod.rs:198); classing those as retryable `server_error` would make configuration errors retry and mislabel them. Severity low agreed: refresh-time failures are a small fraction of outages and the message is still recognisably a network error.
verdicts.corrected_title: A network failure during the lazy token refresh surfaces as non-retryable `token_error` instead of `network_error`: `token_adapter::token_error` flattens `AuthError::Http` like every other non-fatal variant
verdicts.corrected_proposal: In `token_adapter::token_error`, add `AuthError::Http(_) => "network_error"` only (leave `TokenExchange` as `token_error` unless `azapptoolkit-auth` later splits a genuine 5xx variant). In `core::reauth`, add a small `TRANSIENT_PASSTHROUGH: &[&str] = &["network_error"]` (or a `passthrough_any` fn) and have `http_error_enum!`'s `Token(t)` arm and `ExchangeError::ui_code` pass it through alongside the fatal codes so `is_retryable` sees one `network_error` class regardless of hop. Extend the dto `reauth_agreement_tests` (or a new adapter test) to pin that `AuthError::Http` maps to a retryable, non-reauth-fatal code on both planes, noting the intentional `network` (auth plane) vs `network_error` (client plane) spelling.

verdicts.notes: Evidence is real and the premise is false. bulk.rs:125-134 justifies sharing audit_cancel with 'the two long-running loops never run at once', but nothing enforces that: views are keep-alive (web-rs/src/lib.rs:274, 288), audit_view/mod.rs:239-247 mounts a BulkActionBar (RemoveExpired/Delete) inside the Security view whose `busy` (bulk_action_bar.rs:387, 459-461, 620) is independent of the controller's `scanning` (controller.rs:182-185, which never clears `result`, so the table+bar stay live during a re-scan), bulk_actions_view.rs has only its own `busy`, and there is no session-level long-run gate. CancelFlag::cancel (state.rs:94-97) does `cancelled.fetch_max(current)`, so every older generation on the flag stops; the pinning test `cancelling_also_stops_older_runs_still_in_flight` (state.rs:765-776) and the `cancel()` doc justify that only as 'a displaced run stopping is harmless', which assumes same-kind runs. 12 claim sites share the flag (audit.rs:147, bulk.rs:156/319/418/541/616/674/724/774/842/905, aap_migration.rs:52) plus two cancel commands (audit.rs:478, bulk.rs:133). caching-and-search.md:350 records the sharing ('audit_cancel (audit + bulk)') but not the collateral-cancel trade-off, so this is not a documented decision. The secondary point stands too: every BulkActionBar listens to one `bulk-progress` channel (bulk.rs:12-13, bulk_action_bar.rs:391-392), so two concurrent bulk runs interleave. Severity downgraded from high to medium: the collateral stop is clean (item boundary, unattempted apps named, `incomplete`/`cancelled` flagged, nothing cached or corrupted) and needs two concurrent long runs plus a Cancel; it is a real correctness/UX bug in a write path, not data loss. The Minimal (S) proposal (own `bulk_cancel`/`migration_cancel` flags + pin the command→flag mapping in repo_invariants/cancel.rs) is the right shape under repo conventions; the run_id design is optional.

Verified: `throttle_observer: RwLock<Option<Arc<dyn ThrottleObserver>>>` (client.rs:143) with unconditional overwrite/clear (client.rs:262-268); `ThrottleGuard::drop` clears whatever is installed (throttle.rs:140-144) with no identity check; the transport clones the slot per attempt (transport.rs:557) and `$batch` reads it per throttled round (batch.rs:296), so after a foreign clear every later request sees `None`. All six attach sites (audit.rs:133, bulk.rs:185/326/424, sharepoint.rs:864, backup.rs:88) use the shared per-tenant `Arc<GraphClient>` from `state.graph_for`. Concurrency between these runs is real (see finding 0: keep-alive views, per-component busy flags, audit+bulk in one view; site sweep + audit on different views). The guard doc (throttle.rs:126-131) only considers the sequential/early-return case. The one existing observer test (client/tests/transport.rs:~290) attaches a single observer. Not handled elsewhere. Severity honest at medium: the consequence is loss of adaptive back-off (fixed cap, no halving) for the surviving run, while the per-request `with_retries` still honours Retry-After, so it degrades rather than fails — but it defeats the exact contract the guard exists for, and AGENTS.md lists the adaptive throttle as an invariant. Either proposal works; the compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq` against the guard's own tracker, plus a warn when an attach displaces a live observer) is the smaller change; multi-observer `Vec<Weak<_>>` is more correct since Graph pressure on one tenant is genuinely shared. A two-observer transport test is the right pin.

Evidence verified. permission_tester.rs:441-444 asserts 'the two never run concurrently from the UI'; resource_access/mod.rs:19-20 says all panels stay mounted (display toggle) and each gates only on its own signal (sites.rs:186-189 `scanning`, keyvault.rs:190-193 `scanning`, mailboxes.rs:173 `probing`), so a site sweep, a KV sweep and a mailbox probe can all be in flight at once; app_site_access_panel.rs (do_scan gated on its own `scanning`) is a fourth entry point that calls the same `sweep_site_permissions`. Three commands claim `sweep_cancel` (sharepoint.rs:839, permission_tester.rs:456, keyvault_rbac.rs:96 — the docstring's 'both' is already stale) and four frontend handlers call the one `cancel_resource_sweep` (sites.rs:235, keyvault.rs:239, mailboxes.rs:198, app_site_access_panel.rs:138), which stamps `current` so every older generation stops. resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:12-15 and bindings/keyvault_rbac.rs:3 repeat the premise. Cancelled sweeps are deliberately not cached (sharepoint.rs:989-992; sites.rs:127-128 / keyvault.rs:137-138 render the caveat). The duplicate-sweep point is also correct: `single_flight` is used only in search.rs, gallery.rs and applications/cache.rs, never around the sweep. Severity: medium is fair — read-only, so no tenant harm, but a multi-minute tenant-wide sweep is discarded and a false coverage caveat shown; the false premise appears in three places. Proposal is sound; the single-flight wrap must re-check the cache after acquiring the gate (a cancelled first run caches nothing, so the joiner would legitimately re-run).

The cross-cancel is real: dr.rs:55 gates backup on `busy` only, dr.rs:150-155 `do_restore` never reads `busy`, the Restore controls are hidden only while `restoring` (dr.rs:361-366) and the Back-up button disabled only while `busy` (dr.rs:237); both cancel handlers call `cancel_dr` (dr.rs:96-98, 180-182); both commands claim the same `dr_cancel` (backup.rs:78, restore.rs:193) and restore.rs:359 acknowledges the sharing without considering overlap; backup-and-restore.md:126-128/173 only argue dr_cancel vs audit_cancel. But the stated consequence is wrong: restore.rs passes 2-5 each check `is_cancelled()` per item and, per the design comment (restore.rs:184-186) and backup-and-restore.md:173-175, a cancel 'stops creating new apps but still finishes wiring the created ones — never bare shells'; the report says '(cancelled before completing — partial)' (dr.rs:494) and names the apps. So the outcome is a clean, reported partial restore, not stranded shells. Severity lowered to low: the scenario (starting a restore into a tenant while backing it up, then pressing the backup's Cancel) is unusual, and the stop is clean; the fix is still worth making because it is trivial and removes a DR footgun.
verdicts.corrected_title: Backup and restore share dr_cancel and are gated by independent signals in the DR view, so the backup's Cancel also stops an in-flight restore (reported as a partial restore)
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Frontend (S): make the two flows mutually exclusive on the page — disable/hide 'Restore into this tenant…' and 'Load backup file…' while `busy`, and disable 'Back up this tenant' while `restoring`. Optionally backend (S): add `restore_cancel: CancelFlag` + `cancel_restore` command so only the restore's own Cancel can stop the write; update restore.rs:359 and backup-and-restore.md to say backup and restore never overlap (or have separate flags). Drop the 'bare shells' claim — passes 2-5 already finish wiring created apps after a cancel.

verdicts.notes: Verified. aap_migration.rs:36-42 says the operator 'could not stop a whole-tenant migration once started' and claims `audit_cancel` (line 52); the only two frontend callers (exchange_scoping_section.rs:332-338, dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs:69-74) both pass `Some(&app_id)` and neither file contains 'cancel'; the only frontend cancel callers are cancel_audit, cancel_bulk, cancel_resource_sweep and cancel_dr. With `app_id: Some`, `group_policies_for_migration` yields one batch, so the `is_cancelled() || is_dead()` check in the `while let` loop (aap_migration.rs:~95) runs once, before the only write — it can honour a Cancel pressed during the preceding reads (via an unrelated audit/bulk Cancel button) and nothing else. One correction to the rationale: the repo_invariants detector (`dispatch_capped(` / `run_bulk_seq(` / `report.cancelled = true`) does not match this command (it uses a local `cancelled = true` and `incomplete: cancelled`), so the claim here is not actually what satisfies the invariant — removing it would not fail CI, which makes the 'fix the comment vs wire a Cancel' decision purely a product one. The binding accepts `app_id: Option<&str>`, so a whole-tenant run is reachable from code but not from any UI. Proposal is reasonable; if per-app stays the only shape, also consider extending the invariant detector to cover this loop shape.

Asymmetry confirmed: auth.rs:52-53 removes only `graph_clients` and `exchange_clients`; `kv_clients` (keyed per (tenant, vault)), `arm_clients` and `la_clients` (state.rs:207-214) have no references anywhere outside state.rs, so nothing ever removes them. Not a credential leak — `ScopedTokenAdapter::bearer` re-asks the auth singleton per request (token_adapter.rs:69-82), so a stale client fails with not_signed_in. The post-invalidate `cache.put` window (audit.rs:441-446 after `invalidate_tenant`) is real but tiny and requires sign-out to land between the last Graph read and the put. The 'cancel all three flags in sign_out' half of the proposal has a flaw the finding misses: the cancel flags are process-global, not tenant-keyed, while `sign_out` takes one `TenantContext` and AppState is explicitly multi-tenant ('Each signed-in tenant gets its own GraphClient'); `CancelFlag::cancel` stamps the current generation, so signing out tenant A would abort a run on tenant B. Pruning all five maps and adding the repo_invariants check is a clean improvement; the flag cancel should be dropped or made conditional.
verdicts.corrected_title: sign_out prunes only graph_clients and exchange_clients; kv_clients, arm_clients and la_clients survive sign-out
verdicts.corrected_proposal: In sign_out remove the tenant's entries from all five client maps (`kv_clients.lock().retain(|(t, _), _| t != &tenant.tenant_id)`, `arm_clients`/`la_clients` `.remove(&tenant.tenant_id)`) and add a repo_invariants test that every `Mutex<HashMap<…, Arc<…Client>>>` field on AppState is referenced in `sign_out`. Do NOT cancel `audit_cancel`/`sweep_cancel`/`dr_cancel` there unless the flags become tenant-keyed — they are process-global and would abort another signed-in tenant's run; rely on `SessionDead` (the next `bearer()` fails with not_signed_in) as today. If the post-invalidate cache-put window matters, guard the final `cache.put` in run_audit/sweep on the session still being alive rather than cancelling globally.

verdicts.notes: Verified at state.rs:215-227 (finding cites 213-222; content matches). All three field docs still say 'Reset to `false` at the top of every run' / 'Reset at the top of every sweep' / 'Reset at the top of every backup/restore' although `CancelInner`'s doc (state.rs:42-56) explains reset() was removed as a destructive write and `CancelFlag::claim` replaced it. `cancel_site_sweep` appears nowhere in the tree except that comment (the command is `cancel_resource_sweep`, sharepoint.rs:999). `audit_cancel` is also cancelled by `cancel_bulk` (bulk.rs:133) and claimed by all bulk_* commands and the AAP migration; `sweep_cancel` is also claimed by `sweep_key_vault_access` (keyvault_rbac.rs:96) and `find_mailbox_reachers` (permission_tester.rs:456) — none mentioned. The same stale 'reset' wording also survives in backup-and-restore.md:126/173 and audit-findings-and-remediation.md:325 (which the finding attributes to F030). Proposal is correct and cheap; include the `dr_cancel` doc in the rewrite.

Evidence is real: credentials.rs:62-75 scans /applications with a 5-field $select; applications/mod.rs:53-64 list_row_select is a strict superset of that and of the app_name_index projection (cache.rs:334 list_application_index_named = id,appId,displayName); home_dashboard.rs:29/44/69 create the apps/enterprise/creds LocalResources on mount, and enterprise -> list_enterprise_applications -> indexes_cached -> app_name_index_cached (enterprise_application.rs:93, cache.rs:315-337) is a third cold /applications pagination. Both keys are busted by the same two tiers (cache.rs:108+126 in invalidate_app_lists, :149+157 in invalidate_app_credentials; no other invalidator of apps_pairing_key), and mod.rs:181-193 seeds the SP index but never app_name_index. The 150/min keyCredentials throttle note is real (graph client/applications.rs:214). Corrections: (1) the 'contradicts the caching doc' claim is a stretch — caching-and-search.md:35 is about the two lean *indexes*, and credentials.rs:9-16 explicitly documents this as a second scan of the same collection mitigated by caching under the same freshness contract, i.e. a known, partly-deliberate choice rather than an unnoticed violation; (2) the wall-clock benefit is overstated — the three scans already run concurrently, so the credential card does not land 'after its own scan'; the real win is 3x fewer /applications requests (18->6 at 5k apps, 33->11 at 10k), two of them carrying keyCredentials, and less contention with the SP scans and any restored dock fetches — bandwidth/CPU/throttle headroom on very large tenants, not user-visible latency on typical ones, hence severity low; (3) the proposal to have list_credential_expirations 'call the pairing core instead of scanning' cannot work alone: ApplicationListRowDto rows are lean scalars (caching-and-search.md 'Filtering happens in the frontend, on lean rows'), so when apps_pairing is warm but credential_expirations is cold (LRU-evictable per finding 3, or stored at different times) the pairing core returns a hit and yields no credential rows — the credential command must keep its own scan as a fallback; (4) seeding app_name_index from the pairing scan must project down to id/appId/displayName first, or the 'lean' pinned index holds every app's credential arrays in memory for the 60-min TTL; (5) a repo_invariants allowlist of list_applications_all( call sites cuts against the repo's 'derive, don't list' style (fanout.rs:18 already uses that string as a TENANT_WIDE_READ marker).
verdicts.corrected_title: Cold launch runs three concurrent /applications paginations (pairing rows, credential roll-up, app-name index) whose projections nest, and the pairing scan seeds neither of the other two caches
verdicts.corrected_proposal: In list_applications_with_pairing (mod.rs ~157-222): take generation_for watches for app_name_index_key and credential_expirations_key before the scan (alongside the existing apps_pairing watch); after the scan, store (a) a lean projection of the apps (id/app_id/display_name only, ..Default::default()) via app_name_index_store_if_current, and (b) summarize_credentials rows (factor the row build out of credentials.rs into a shared fn) via put_index_if_current under credential_expirations_key. In list_credential_expirations and app_name_index_cached, before their own scan, acquire-and-release state.single_flight(&apps_pairing_key(tenant)) so a pairing scan in flight lands first, then re-check their own cache and fall back to their existing scan on a miss (the pairing rows cannot rebuild the credential roll-up). Expected effect: on a cold tenant the launch costs one /applications pagination instead of three; warm/partial cases are unchanged. Drop the allowlist pin; the existing watch-capture-order invariant already covers the new stores.

verdicts.notes: All cited evidence checks out: open_items_workspace.rs:131 mounts the overlay whenever open_items is non-empty (independent of shown_items), :138 keyed <For> mounts a window per item, :238 hides by style:display; tenant.rs:38 calls restore_open_items() inside set_active_tenant (which runs at sign-in/session restore — CHANGELOG line 32 confirms the session is restored at launch and line 86 confirms the dock is 'parked per tenant across restarts'); open_items.rs:217-218 + :240 restore open_items with shown_items deliberately empty. views/application_detail_pane.rs:39-51 creates the detail LocalResource unconditionally on mount (enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:104 likewise), and get_application_detail (mod.rs:252-282) is the 4-wave fan-out described. frontend-workspace.md:124-126 documents mount-all for chip-switch reuse only; nothing documents restore-time eager fetching, and no GUI test covers the restore path (tests/gui/open_items_dock.rs has no restore/parked case, though its mock_details at :47-50 mocks get_application_detail so an invoke-count assertion is straightforward). The proposed building block exists: util.rs:24 keep_alive is a Show-when-visited latch. MAX_OPEN_ITEMS = 8 (open_items.rs:19) and restore does not clamp, so the worst case is 8 hidden panes. Only caveat (not a refutation): the eager fetch does warm the backend app_detail| cache so a later chip click is instant — a trade-off worth a design note, but the operator lands on Home per the restore comment, so paying ~40 Graph calls plus 8 detail payloads before any pane is visible, concurrently with Home's tenant-wide scans, is the wrong default. Severity medium is fair for a full dock; with 1-2 parked items the cost is minor.

Premise verified: home_dashboard.rs:84-96 fetches get_cached_audit and :416/:424 use only posture_counts(&r.items) and ranked_actionable_findings(&r.items) (groups.rs:216-224 -> group_findings, counts + worst severity per group); audit_view/controller.rs:28/:131 holds its own full copy; commands/audit.rs:501-513 reads CachedAuditRun through the untyped cache.get (cache.rs:657-665 deserializes the Arc<Value> tree into Vec<AuditItem> on every call) and then Tauri re-serializes it for IPC. AuditItem has 21 pub fields incl. five Vecs (core/audit/types.rs:514-557). The codebase itself treats this vector as 'multi-MB' and already avoids shipping it for export (audit.rs save_audit_to_file doc: 'the multi-MB item vector never round-trips the IPC bridge') and in the controller ('without cloning the multi-MB run'), so Home's whole-run read is inconsistent with the repo's own judgment. Corrections to the proposal: (1) do NOT store the audit run via put_typed_index_if_current — CacheKind::Audit holds one entry per tenant in its own bucket (cap MAX_CACHE_SIZE, nothing evicts it), pinning buys nothing, and repo_invariants/cache.rs pinned_cache_writes_stay_on_the_tenant_wide_indexes would flag a pinned write whose key builder (audit_cache_key) is not in PINNABLE_KEYS; use plain put_typed/get_typed (cache.rs:864/:924) and switch all three access sites together (run_audit :441-447, get_cached_audit :504, save_audit_to_file :558) since a typed entry read untyped is a documented silent miss; (2) the 'four other cards' half is weak — ApplicationListRowDto is already lean scalars by design (caching-and-search.md 'Filtering happens in the frontend, on lean rows') and the Apps list needs those rows anyway, enterprise/MI rows come from the lean SP index projection, so an inventory-summary command saves little; keep the finding to the audit run; (3) moving group_findings' GroupSpec table into core is a larger refactor than moving posture_counts — a summary DTO keyed by the existing issue:: constants (already in core) is enough for Home.
verdicts.corrected_title: Home ships the entire cached audit run (10k AuditItems, five Vecs each) over IPC and holds a second WASM copy just to render posture counts
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Add a get_cached_audit_summary command (session-proved like get_cached_audit) returning { completed_at, posture: PostureCounts, groups: Vec<{key, worst_level, count}> }; move posture_counts (web-rs views/audit_view/posture.rs) into azapptoolkit-core::audit so Home, the Security strip and the backend share one count source, and derive the group rows from the issue:: constants already in core. Switch Home's cached_audit resource to the summary. Store CachedAuditRun with put_typed and read it with get_typed at all three sites (run_audit, get_cached_audit, save_audit_to_file) so the backend read is a refcount clone, not a Value-tree walk — unpinned, since CacheKind::Audit is a one-entry-per-tenant bucket. Leave the four inventory cards as they are.

verdicts.notes: credentials.rs:97 is a plain state.cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, ...), while core/cache.rs:711-720 (put_index doc) explicitly lists 'the credential-expiry roll-up' among the pinned tenant-wide indexes — so the doc claims a pin the code does not have. The eviction mechanism is real: the Lists bucket is capped at MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE = 10,000 (cache.rs:601-603, constants.rs:70) and shares that cap with per-app app_detail| writes (mod.rs:292) and per-app mail_scopes|audit|{app}| writes the audit makes (exchange/mail_scopes.rs:249-254, plus declared|/held| variants), so a mail-heavy audit or heavy browsing on a large tenant can LRU-evict the unpinned roll-up within its 60-min TTL and force a silent full /applications rescan for the Home card and the Credential Expiry tab — exactly the scenario the put_index doc describes. The sibling list stores (enterprise_application.rs:115, managed_identity.rs:88, mod.rs:220) all use put_index_if_current, so this is the one outlier. Two small corrections to the proposal: the repo_invariants pin does not keep a per-key list for the _if_current forms (cache.rs:130-145 skips them; the watch-capture-order test covers them), so no PINNABLE_KEYS/allowlist edit is needed — just take generation_for(CacheKind::Lists, &cache_key) before the .await at credentials.rs:62 and store via put_index_if_current(watch, &rows); and the 'found >= 5' floor in pinned_cache_writes_stay_on_the_tenant_wide_indexes simply counts one more. Severity low is honest (a redundant rescan, no wrong data). If finding 0 is adopted the store moves into the pairing core with its own watch.

Verified: apps/desktop/web-rs/Trunk.toml has no minify key (its comment covers only the --release/optimization default); upstream trunk-rs/trunk main Trunk.toml documents `minify = "never" # can be one of: never, on_release, always` as the default; the justfile web-build-release and web-build-pages recipes pass --release --locked with no --minify; grep finds no minify anywhere in the repo; index.html tunes wasm-opt=z and Cargo.toml [profile.release] sets opt-level z / lto / codegen-units 1 / strip, so the wasm side is tuned while CSS (styles.css = 120,706 bytes) and the wasm-bindgen JS glue ship verbatim; GUI tests build via cargo test/wasm-pack, not Trunk, so they are unaffected, and on_release leaves trunk serve alone. One nuance on the secondary 'pin Trunk' step: taiki-e/install-action is pinned by SHA (v2.87.17) in ci.yml:152, pages.yml:44 and release.yml:131, and that action bundles its tool manifests, so the trunk version CI installs is already implicitly fixed by the action pin (it moves only when the action is bumped); an explicit `trunk@x.y.z` would make it visible but is not strictly needed. Dev boxes (scripts/setup.sh:66 `cargo install trunk --locked`) are the genuinely unpinned path. Severity low is honest — assets load from the local asset protocol, so this is parse/startup and bundle-size hygiene, not a user-visible regression.

Premise verified: justfile web-itest-size measures only target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/deps/gui_*.wasm against a 52 MB ceiling; web-build-release prints nothing; ci.yml:177 is the only size step and it is that shard gate; release.yml and pages.yml have no size reporting; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md mention only the ~127 MB WebView2 runtime and CHANGELOG baking — no figure for the shipped .wasm/.js/.css exists anywhere. So there is no baseline and a regression would land silently. The proposal needs one correction: wiring web-size into verify-full would force a release Trunk build (lto + opt-level z + wasm-opt z, minutes) that verify-full does not run today (_verify-core ends with the debug web-build) and that CI does not run as a gate either — the justfile's own comment (justfile ~323-329) insists verify-full mirror CI exactly, so adding a local-only step there violates that contract. Also, the Pages bundle includes the demo feature and its fixtures, so it is not the shipped artifact; the true number comes from the release.yml legs (dist exists after cargo tauri build's beforeBuildCommand) and is identical across the 3-OS matrix, so report it once. Severity low is honest.

verdicts.corrected_proposal: Add a `web-size` recipe (Unix/CI like web-itest-size) that prints raw and gzip byte sizes of apps/desktop/web-rs/dist/*.wasm, *.js and *.css and requires an existing dist (no rebuild). Call it from release.yml on one leg (e.g. Linux, after the build step) and from pages.yml after web-build-pages, appending to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; do not add it to verify-full (it would break the recipe's CI-parity contract and add a minutes-long release build). Record today's release-build numbers in docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md next to the bundle/crypto notes, and optionally have web-size warn (not fail) past ~1.5x that wasm baseline via an env-overridable threshold.

verdicts.notes: All quoted evidence is real. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-37 and :44-49 call `updater.check()` with no install-format gate. Vendored tauri-plugin-updater 2.12.0 src/updater.rs:581-582 computes `installer_for_bundle_type(bundle_type())` and `get_urls` (:608-635) falls back from `{os}-{arch}-{installer}` to the bare `{os}-{arch}` key; release.yml:213-215 publishes only bare keys, so an MSI or .deb install always gets `Some(update)`. Linux `install_inner` (:1045-1049) dispatches on `bundle_type()` and `install_deb` (:1126-1131) rejects AppImage bytes with `InvalidUpdaterFormat` only after the full download; Windows `extract_exe` (:994-1003) classifies by bytes so NSIS bytes run `setup.exe /P /UPDATE` via ShellExecuteW (:841-880) on top of a per-machine MSI. `tauri_utils::platform::bundle_type()` exists at tauri-utils-2.9.3/src/platform.rs:353-368 and is reachable as `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type` (tauri-2.11.6/src/lib.rs:115). The only documented mitigation (README.md:196-198, :255-259, archived CHANGELOG line 3286) is the `auto_update` opt-out, and `UserSettings::load` / `.auto_update` have zero callers outside crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs, so the README's 'disable auto-update on MSI installs' advice is inert. Not a documented deliberate decision: README/release body/CHANGELOG state the *policy* that MSI/.deb are not auto-updated, but nothing enforces it. update_splash.rs:40-43 does surface the raw plugin message. The GUI shell test (web-rs/tests/gui/shell.rs:21-24) deliberately leaves `check_for_update` unmocked, so mocking a tri-state DTO is feasible. Severity: high is defensible because the toast actively invites the wrong install on every launch with no warning, though the harm still needs two clicks (toast -> 'Update & restart'); medium-high would also be honest. Proposal is sound; the gate must only fire on `Some(Msi|Deb|Rpm)` since `bundle_type()` is `None` for dev/unbundled binaries.

Evidence checks out. release.yml:105-108 uses floating `ubuntu-latest` for the Linux leg; docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:13 just restates `ubuntu-latest`, and no doc, CHANGELOG or workflow mentions glibc or a distro floor. Reproduced the objdump on this Ubuntu 24.04 / glibc 2.39 box: target/debug/deps/azapptoolkit_auth-* imports strong `(GLIBC_2.38) __isoc23_sscanf` / `__isoc23_strtol` (the core-only binary tops out at 2.34 strong, so the 2.38 floor comes from the C deps — aws-lc-sys 0.45.0 via rustls/reqwest, and src-tauri/Cargo.toml:63 links aws-lc-rs directly, so the shipped desktop binary carries at least the same floor). README.md:225-229 and release.yml:312 promise 'runs on most distributions'; the Tauri .deb declares unversioned depends so it installs and then fails at exec on Ubuntu 22.04 (2.35) / Debian 12 (2.36) / RHEL 9 (2.34). Caveats the verdict should carry: (a) the release binary itself was not inspected here — the floor is inferred from a workspace test binary with the same C deps, which is a safe inference but not an observation; (b) jammy does ship `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`, so the `ubuntu-22.04` pin is feasible, but GitHub-hosted 22.04 images have a finite life (standard support ends 2027), so the proposed objdump guard step is the load-bearing, durable part and should fail the job rather than warn. Tauri's own v2 CI guidance builds Linux on `ubuntu-22.04`. Severity high is honest for a shipped .deb/AppImage that cannot start on current LTS distros the README targets.

Quoted lines are real: README.md:217-219 ('updates in place like the Windows NSIS build'), crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/token_cache.rs:54-56 registers `apple_native_keyring_store::keychain::Store` (legacy `SecKeychain*` generic-password API, vendored apple-native-keyring-store-1.0.2/src/keychain.rs:72-74), docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:161-164 says unsigned/not notarized, and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:36-42 maps every restore error (incl. `AuthError::Keyring` -> code `keyring`, dto/lib.rs:168) to `Ok(None)` with an info-level log. The vendored plugin's macOS `install_inner` (tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0/src/updater.rs:1294-1385) does replace the whole `.app` by rename, so the post-update binary is a new code object. The ACL premise matches Apple's legacy-keychain trusted-application model (unsigned or linker ad-hoc-signed binaries have no stable designated requirement, so the trust entry is bound to the binary hash) — the reviewer correctly flags this as reasoned, not observed on hardware, and the docs wording should hedge accordingly ('macOS may ask for keychain access again after an update'). Nothing in README/DEVELOPMENT/architecture docs mentions Keychain prompts or 'Always Allow' (grep confirms). Small corrections: the misleading hint text is the frontend's own string at web-rs/src/views/sign_in.rs:157-158 ('unlock your keychain/credential manager'), not keyring-crate text; and the optional 'stored version differs' warn-log would need a version field that settings.json does not currently persist. Severity medium is fair for a docs gap that produces a confusing post-update sign-in with a wrong hint; category docs is right.

Evidence is accurate: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:395-399 resolves `config_directory()` from `%APPDATA%` (Roaming) on Windows and :391-393 puts logs under it; the default filter at :330-331 is `azapptoolkit=debug,desktop=debug` with 14 daily files (:354); README.md:426 documents `%APPDATA%\azapptoolkit\logs`. Tauri's own convention is verified in vendored tauri-2.11.6/src/path/desktop.rs:278-290: `app_log_dir` = `dirs::data_local_dir()/<identifier>/logs` (LOCALAPPDATA) on Windows/Linux and `~/Library/Logs/<identifier>` on macOS. The lib.rs comment (:333-337) states the paths with no roaming rationale, and no doc, CHANGELOG or .claude/rules entry records a decision to roam logs, so this is a convention slip rather than a deliberate choice. Not pinned by any repo_invariants test. Severity downgraded from medium to low: the harm (profile bloat / slower logon / GUID-bearing logs following the user) is real but modest and confined to roaming-profile / FSLogix estates, and it is an enhancement, not a defect. The proposal is reasonable and self-contained (keep settings.json in Roaming, move only logs, update README Logs + the lib.rs comment, CHANGELOG note because the documented support path changes); a best-effort one-time move is optional.

Confirmed docs contradiction. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:179-181 says the NSIS installer 'asks once about per-user vs per-machine'; apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:38-42 sets no `bundle.windows.nsis.installMode`, and updater-build.json only sets `createUpdaterArtifacts`. Vendored tauri-utils-2.9.3/src/config.rs:819-841 shows `NSISInstallerMode` defaults to `CurrentUser` and only `Both` offers the chooser (and `Both` 'will require Administrator access even if the user wants to install it for the current user only' — so the doc's implied no-admin tester flow is impossible under the chooser anyway). README.md:189-190, release.yml:295 and DEVELOPMENT.md:137 all say per-user/no admin, so :180 is the odd one out. One overstatement in the rationale: switching to `both` would not outright 'break' passive updates — the NSIS `/P /UPDATE` relaunch would trigger a UAC prompt rather than fail silently — but the doc fix is still correct and the warning against flipping the mode is worth keeping in softer form. Severity low, one-line docs edit; the optional repo_invariants pin is cheap but not required.
